title: Sr. Manager, Data Engineering
desc:
Role Summary We're looking for a Senior Manager to lead a blended AI engineering team building the agentic AI platform and the marketing solutions that run on top of it. This is a delivery-leadership role: you own the roadmap, execution, and quality bar for a team of platform engineers, applied-AI solutions builders, and data engineering — turning cutting-edge agentic AI into reliable, production systems that marketing and analytics teams depend on every day.
 You will operate at the intersection of platform and product: hardening the agentic infrastructure (LLM orchestration, retrieval, tool/MCP integration, deploys, reliability) while making sure the AI solutions built on it deliver real marketing outcomes. You'll grow the people on your team, set a high engineering bar, and partner across a global AI organization.
 What You'll Do Platform & infrastructure 
 Own delivery and reliability of the agentic AI platform: LLM orchestration, retrieval/RAG pipelines, tool and MCP integration, model routing, and evaluation.
 Drive engineering quality — test discipline, deployment safety, observability, cost and latency management — across everything the team ships.
 Set technical direction with your senior engineers; make the hard architecture calls and unblock the team (design-level involvement; not expected to write production code day-to-day).
 Applied AI solutions 
 Lead the team that builds AI agents and workflows for marketing use cases (analytics, paid media, content-to-intent, executive reporting) on top of the platform.
 Ensure solutions are grounded in real business outcomes and adopted by stakeholders — not demos that stall.
 Balance platform investment against solution delivery so both advance.
 People leadership & delivery 
 Manage, coach, and grow a blended team; run hiring to build out the function.
 Own the roadmap and quarterly planning; convert ambiguous priorities into committed, sequenced delivery.
 Represent the team's work to leadership and cross-functional partners; drive alignment across a globally distributed AI organization.
 The Team You'll Lead A blended engineering team of:
 Agentic AI / platform engineers — Python, LLM orchestration, RAG, MCP/tooling, cloud-native deploys.
 Applied-AI solutions builders — wiring AI to marketing and analytics use cases.
 Data engineering — the pipelines and semantic layer the AI grounds on.
 Must-Have Qualifications ~12+ years in software / AI/ML engineering, with 4+ years managing engineering teams (including hiring and growing engineers).
 Demonstrated depth in agentic AI / LLM systems — orchestration, retrieval/RAG, tool use, agent frameworks, and evaluation of AI quality.
 Track record of shipping production AI/ML systems at scale — reliability, deployment safety, cost/latency awareness — not just prototypes.
 Strong Python and modern cloud-native / containerized delivery.
 Ability to set a high engineering bar and make sound architecture decisions while leading primarily through the team.
 Excellent communication and stakeholder management across a globally distributed organization.
 Preferred Qualifications Marketing technology or analytics domain experience — AEP / AJO / CJA, adtech, or digital marketing analytics.
 Experience with Databricks, vector databases (pgvector), graph stores (Neo4j), or similar data/AI infrastructure.
 Hands-on with agent/LLM frameworks and MCP, prompt/eval tooling, and LLM cost governance.
 Experience standing up or scaling a new AI engineering function.
 What Success Looks Like (First 6–12 Months) A team operating with a clear roadmap, predictable delivery, and a visibly higher quality/reliability bar.
 At least one AI solution moved from concept to in-production use, adopted by marketing/analytics stakeholders.
 Platform reliability, evaluation, and cost/observability practices established as the default, not the exception.
 Key hires made; team members growing and taking on larger scope.
 Leadership Behaviors Candor and clarity — lead with the bottom line, disagree openly, separate fact from guess, flag risks early.
 Ownership — own outcomes end-to-end, not just handoffs; the team ships things that work and says so honestly when they don't.
 Bar-raiser — hire people better than the current team and hold a high engineering standard.
 Builder's bias — move fast on real problems, cut scope ruthlessly, prefer working systems over polished plans.

The right person develops talent, embeds AI into how the team works, holds a high standard on delivery quality, and represents the practice with credibility to customers and senior stakeholders. The Opportunity   
 Customer Experience Orchestration (CXO) is a key part of Adobe’s strategy to help enterprises deliver personalized and connected customer experiences at scale.   
 We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead a strong engineering team within Adobe Campaign, with a primary focus on driving the product's security strategy and initiatives while providing broader technical and people leadership.   
 The Challenge   
 As an Engineering Manager, you will lead technical execution, people development, and strategic engineering initiatives. Your role will focus on:   
 Security Leadership: Own and drive key security initiatives for Adobe Campaign, working closely with Security and engineering teams to identify risks, prioritize remediation, and continuously strengthen the product's security posture.   
 Technical Leadership: Drive architecture and technical decisions for complex, scalable, and reliable systems.   
 People Leadership: Mentor and develop engineers, support career growth, and build a high-performing engineering team.   
 Engineering Excellence: Drive high standards across software quality, reliability, performance, operational excellence, and engineering practices.   
 Product Leadership: Partner with Product, Architecture, Quality Engineering, Security, and other stakeholders to translate business and customer needs into effective technical solutions.   
 Roles & Responsibilities   
 Lead, mentor, and develop a team of software engineers.   
 Own and drive the security charter for Adobe Campaign , including security improvements, vulnerability remediation, and collaboration with internal security organizations.   
 Provide technical direction and oversight across the team's engineering initiatives.   
 Drive scalable, reliable, and maintainable solutions through strong engineering practices and technical decision-making.   
 Partner with cross-functional teams to define priorities, manage execution, and deliver high-quality outcomes.   
 Identify and address technical, operational, and architectural challenges.   
 Drive continuous improvement across engineering processes, systems, and team practices.   
 Participate in hiring and career development of engineers.   
 Work effectively with geographically distributed teams in a fast-paced Agile environment.   
 Required Skills & Expertise   
 8+ years of software engineering experience, including experience managing engineering teams.   
 Strong understanding of microservices, distributed systems, cloud architecture, design patterns, and frameworks.   
 Strong computer science fundamentals and system design experience.   
 Application security & vulnerability management for enterprise SaaS: Experience with threat modelling , secure code review, source/sink/escaper taint analysis, and remediation of OWASP Top 10 and related vulnerability classes, including injection, broken authentication/authorization, CSRF, SSRF, XXE, XSS, and multi-stage pre-auth RCE chains across native C++, server-side JavaScript, web, and SOAP/REST surfaces.

 Experience with AWS and/or Azure and modern engineering tools and practices.

 Experience building scalable and reliable enterprise software.   
 Strong communication , collaboration, and problem-solving skills.   
 Bachelor's degree or equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.   
 Preferred Qualifications   
 Experience driving security initiatives for enterprise software products.   
 Familiarity with security scanning, CVE remediation, threat modeling , authentication/authorization, or security compliance.   
 Experience working with large-scale enterprise SaaS products.

title: LLM & Agentic AI Performance Engineer
desc:
Job Details: 
 Job Description:  The Role and Impact: 
Join Intel's Data Center AI organization and help shape how LLM and Agentic AI workloads perform on Intel platforms.
 Our team operates at a unique intersection of core performance optimization, AI frameworks, and customer-facing AI solutions. We bridge the gap between teams that deeply understand silicon and benchmarking and teams building real-world AI solutions, turning performance insights into software optimizations that developers and customers can use.
 In this role, you will own end-to-end performance characterization and optimization of LLM and Agentic AI workloads, from Python-level frameworks and inference runtimes down to Linux, system architecture, and hardware performance counters.
 This is not simply a benchmarking role. Benchmarking tells us what the number is. Your job is to understand why the number is what it is, identify the hardware or software bottleneck, and determine what needs to change to remove it.
 Your work will translate into code contributions, framework optimizations, best-known configurations (BKCs), customer-ready solutions, and insights that help influence future Intel hardware and software.
 If you enjoy working across the complete AI stack, from agent frameworks and LLM serving engines to NUMA, memory bandwidth, cache behavior, and silicon counters, this role provides an opportunity to work at that intersection.
 About the Team: 
The AI Solutions and Toolkit Engineering team is part of Intel's Data Center organization, focused on enabling modern AI workloads and solutions on Intel platforms.
 We work across the AI ecosystem, collaborating with AI framework and runtime developers, performance and optimization teams, hardware architects, open-source communities, and solution engineering teams.
 Our goal is to take deep platform capabilities and performance insights and translate them into practical, optimized AI solutions that developers and customers can deploy.
 The team works across areas including LLM inference, Agentic AI, AI frameworks and runtimes, workload optimization, open-source software, and datacenter AI systems.
 Key Responsibilities: 
 ·   Characterize and optimize LLM and Agentic AI workloads across the complete software and hardware stack.
 ·   Identify performance bottlenecks across AI frameworks, inference runtimes, operating systems, memory, compute, and platform architecture.
 ·   Design and develop hardware-aware and hardware-agnostic optimizations for AI frameworks and runtimes.
 ·   Optimize LLM inference techniques including KV-cache management, attention, continuous batching, and quantization.
 ·   Work hands-on with serving stacks such as vLLM, SGLang, TGI, or equivalent technologies.
 ·   Analyze host and accelerator performance using tools such as VTune, EMON/PMU, perf, top-down analysis, and roofline modeling.
 ·   Debug complex performance issues spanning Python frameworks, native code, Linux, runtime libraries, and hardware.
 ·   Convert performance findings into software changes, upstream contributions, BKCs, and reusable optimization guidance.
 ·   Collaborate with open-source communities to upstream and integrate performance improvements.
 Translate silicon-level findings into actionable recommendations for framework developers, while bringing application and framework insights back to Intel platform and silicon teams.
 Qualifications: Minimum Qualifications: 
 ·   BE +10 years / M.Tech +8 years in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related discipline.
 ·   Significant hands-on experience in performance engineering, systems optimization, or workload characterization on server-class platforms.
 ·   Demonstrated ability to identify complex performance bottlenecks and deliver measurable performance improvements.
 ·   Strong programming skills in Python and C++, or equivalent systems programming experience in C/Rust.
 ·   Strong understanding of server architecture including cache hierarchy, memory bandwidth, NUMA, interconnects, and system-level performance behavior.
 ·   Hands-on experience with Linux performance and system technologies such as affinity, huge pages, cgroups, eBPF, ftrace, perf, or equivalent tools.
 Preferred Qualifications: 
 ·   Deep understanding of LLM inference, including KV-cache, paged attention, continuous batching and quantization such as INT8, INT4, or FP8.
 ·   Hands-on experience modifying or optimizing AI serving stacks such as vLLM, SGLang, TGI, OpenVINO, or equivalent.
 ·   Experience building, profiling, or optimizing Agentic AI systems using technologies such as LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, MCP-based frameworks, or similar platforms.
 ·   Experience with hardware counter-level performance analysis using VTune, EMON/PMU, perf, top-down analysis, or roofline modeling.
 ·   Contributions to significant open-source projects, including upstream code contributions.
 ·   Ability to communicate across abstraction layers, translating silicon-level findings for software developers and application-level requirements for hardware architects.
 Why Join This Team? 
 This role gives you the opportunity to work across boundaries that few engineering positions span:
 Agentic AI & LLMs → AI frameworks → inference runtimes Linux → server architecture → silicon 
 You won't be limited to measuring performance or optimizing an isolated component. You'll help connect the entire stack, identify where the real bottlenecks are, implement improvements, and make those optimizations available to developers and customers.
 The result is tangible: better AI performance today, stronger software solutions for customers, and insights that can influence tomorrow's Intel platforms.

title: AI System Performance Architect
desc:
Job Details: 
 Job Description:  About the Role 
We are looking for a talented and motivated AI System Performance Architect. The role owns the end-to-end understanding of AI training and inference systems, sitting where serving strategy, parallelism, collective communication, and interconnect behavior come together. Through analytical modelling and multi-GPU simulation, the candidate translates SLA and deployment targets into concrete architectural guidance for Intel's future AI platforms. Strong analytical skills and the ability to present performance findings and configuration recommendations to engineering and leadership teams are essential.
 Key Responsibilities 
• Own end-to-end understanding of the AI training/inference system and build analytical models and multi-GPU simulation - including MPI/collective communication (allgather, allreduce, all-to-all) and interconnect contention - to project performance, expose architectural bottlenecks, and recommend optimal Intel system configurations.
• Model inferencing strategies - static batching, continuous batching, disaggregated serving, and chunked prefill - across frameworks such as vLLM and SGLang, covering agentic inferencing, prefix caching, and multi-turn flows.
• Cover data, pipeline, tensor, and expert parallelism and their communication patterns.
• Drive studies against SLA targets - batch size, TTFT, TPOT, ISL/OSL, and TPS.
• Analyse regression run traces and find patterns in utilization counters across SLA operating points to identify architectural bottlenecks.
• Perform what-if analysis by sweeping core count, memory/cache capacity and bandwidth, fabric bandwidth, GPU interconnect, and deployment options; deliver optimization and optimal architecture recommendations.
• Scout whitepapers, blogs, and conferences; keep self and team updated on AI innovations applicable to Intel's end-to-end system.
 Qualifications: Required Qualifications 
• Bachelor's, master's or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.

• Strong proficiency in Python, with the ability to build modular, maintainable analytical models and simulation frameworks.
• Solid understanding of LLM inference and training mechanics: prefill vs. decode, KV cache, batching policies, and quantization.

title: GPU Architecture and AI Performance Simulation Engineer
desc:
Job Details: 
 Job Description:  About the Role 
We are looking for a talented and motivated GPU Architecture and AI Performance Simulation Engineer. The role sits at the intersection of AI workloads and next-generation GPU hardware - analyzing, modeling, and optimizing AI workload performance on GPU and SoC architectures to shape architectural decisions across current and future silicon. The candidate will guide the team in fine-tuning workload, SoC, and system models, propose data-backed architectural enhancements, and track the AI GPU market to inform Intel's future accelerator roadmap. Strong analytical skills, the ability to present performance findings and trade-offs to engineering and leadership teams, and a willingness to mentor peers are essential.
Key Responsibilities 
• Analyze AI workload behavior on GPU architectures - distinguishing compute-bound, memory-bound, and cache-bound behavior to identify performance bottlenecks and optimization opportunities.
• Build and maintain roofline analytical models and cycle-accurate performance models to support hardware what-if studies and guide micro-architectural decisions.
• Analyze AI workloads built on Transformer and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures, inference and training, and assess the hardware-utilization impact of kernel-level optimizations such as Flash Attention, Flash Decode, Sparse Attention, and Causal Masking.
• Model and analyze multi-GPU and at-scale AI systems - workload distribution, synchronization overhead, and communication-compute overlap.
• Drive workload and architectural bottleneck analysis for the early architecture definition phases of Intel's future AI GPU accelerator roadmap products.
• Guide and mentor the team in delivering analytical models and end-to-end system-level performance projections; review modeling methodology and drive consistency across studies.
• Propose new architectural enhancement ideas, backed by quantitative modeling data and workload evidence.
• Maintain a forward-looking view of the AI GPU and accelerator market - tracking competitive roadmaps, whitepapers, and conferences - and translate those trends into architectural requirements while keeping the team updated on applicable AI innovations.
 Qualifications: Required Qualifications 
• Bachelor's with 10+ yrs, master’s with 8+ years and Ph.D with 5+ years of experience in System/GPU/SoC performance engineering, AI workload analysis, or hardware architecture.
• Deep knowledge of GPU microarchitecture (NVIDIA SM/CUDA cores, Intel Xe cores, or equivalent), GPU execution pipelines, and cache hierarchy design (L1/L2/L3).
• Familiarity with SoC design principles, on-chip fabric, memory subsystems, and interconnects.
• Experience with multi-GPU system architectures (NVLink, PCIe, CXL, or equivalent) and scaling AI workloads across multiple devices.
• Good understanding of distributed training/inference techniques: Tensor Parallel, Data Parallel, Pipeline Parallel, Expert Parallel, and Model Split methodologies.
Good-to-Have Skills 
• Experience with cycle-accurate simulators or hardware performance emulation platforms.

• Experience with performance profiling tools (e.g., NVIDIA Nsight, Intel VTune, AMD ROCProfiler, or similar).
• Publications or patents in GPU architecture, AI systems performance, or related areas.

title: Silicon Domain Architect
desc:
Job Details: 
 Job Description:  About the Role and Team
The AI Silicon Architecture and Performance Engineering team is responsible for developing and maintaining performance models that enable architecture exploration, design evaluation, scalability analysis, and performance projection for next-generation AI silicon products. These models are a critical component of the product development process, providing early visibility into architectural tradeoffs, bottlenecks, and optimization opportunities long before silicon availability.
We are seeking a highly experienced and motivated engineer to drive AI silicon performance modeling, validation, architectural analysis, and stakeholder engagement activities. The candidate will work closely with architects, performance stimulus generation teams, silicon design teams, and product stakeholders to evaluate and optimize key AI silicon subsystems that determine overall platform scalability and performance.
The role focuses on performance modeling and analysis of AI SoC communication fabrics, memory subsystems, scale-up and scale-out interconnects, host-device memory paths, and end-to-end data movement infrastructure. The successful candidate will leverage SystemC/TLM-based modeling methodologies to generate actionable insights that directly influence architecture and product decisions.
This position requires a unique combination of software development expertise, architecture understanding, analytical problem solving, and cross-functional technical leadership. The engineer will be expected to independently drive complex technical initiatives while serving as a trusted performance expert across multiple organizations.
________________________________________
Key Responsibilities
1. AI Silicon Performance Model Development
• Develop, maintain, and enhance SystemC/TLM-based performance models representing critical AI silicon subsystems.
• Drive modeling of key architectural components including:
o SoC fabrics and on-chip communication networks
o Memory controllers and memory subsystem behavior
o Scale-up controllers and fabrics enabling accelerator-to-accelerator communication within a node, tray, or pod
o Scale-out controllers and fabrics enabling communication across nodes, racks, and larger AI clusters
o Host CPU to accelerator memory paths
o Local, host, and remote memory access paths
o End-to-end data movement architectures
• Implement new architectural features and capabilities based on evolving product requirements.
• Improve model fidelity, scalability, maintainability, and simulation performance.
• Perform detailed debugging and root-cause analysis of model issues and performance anomalies.
• Contribute to the evolution of modeling infrastructure, methodologies, and best practices.
________________________________________
2. Functional Validation and Model Correlation
• Define and execute comprehensive validation strategies to ensure correctness and architectural accuracy of performance models.
• Develop validation plans, regression suites, coverage methodologies, and quality metrics.
• Correlate modeled behavior against architectural expectations, reference simulations, performance projections, and available hardware measurements.
• Investigate and resolve discrepancies between expected and observed behavior.
• Establish robust validation frameworks that improve stakeholder confidence in model-generated performance projections.
• Continuously improve validation methodologies and model quality.
________________________________________
3. AI Silicon Performance Characterization and Architectural Analysis
• Design and execute performance studies covering a wide range of workloads, traffic patterns, and system configurations.
• Analyze performance of communication fabrics, memory systems, and data movement paths under representative AI workloads.
• Evaluate bandwidth utilization, latency characteristics, congestion behavior, traffic distribution, buffering efficiency, and resource utilization.
• Characterize interactions across local memory, host memory, and remote memory domains.
• Assess scalability of scale-up and scale-out architectures across increasingly larger deployment footprints.
• Identify performance bottlenecks and quantify their impact on overall system throughput and efficiency.
• Conduct architectural tradeoff studies to evaluate alternative design approaches.
• Provide performance-driven recommendations that influence architecture and product decisions.
________________________________________
4. Performance Data Generation, Analytics and Visualization
• Develop frameworks and methodologies for large-scale performance data generation and analysis.
• Create automated workflows for data collection, processing, correlation, and reporting.
• Develop performance dashboards and visualization tools that simplify interpretation of complex performance data.
• Define and track meaningful performance KPIs and architectural metrics.
• Utilize Python-based analysis frameworks to process large datasets and generate actionable insights.
• Enable efficient consumption of performance information by architects, designers, and engineering leadership.
________________________________________
5. Cross-Functional Technical Leadership and Stakeholder Engagement
• Partner closely with architecture teams, performance stimulus generation teams, silicon design teams, and product stakeholders.
• Drive technical discussions related to performance methodology, architectural assumptions, workload behavior, scalability analysis, and bottleneck identification.
• Review architectural proposals and provide performance-driven feedback.
• Present performance studies, technical findings, and architectural recommendations to engineering leadership.
• Influence product and architecture decisions through data-backed analysis and sound engineering judgment.
• Act as a key technical bridge between architecture, modeling, and performance analysis organizations.

title: System and Hardware Enabling Engineer
desc:
Job Details: 
 Job Description:  Intel Edge Computing Engineering Team is on a mission to enable successful ODMs and customers in India to develop differentiated Edge products based on Intel technologies. 
 The team is looking for an experienced Digital Design Engineer with strong board-level hardware design, design-review, hardware-enabling and debug expertise to support customers developing platforms based on Intel Core and Atom processors. 
 The engineer will work closely with customer hardware teams through the complete board design and enabling lifecycle, including schematic design and review, high-speed interface implementation, PCB layout review, prototype board bring-up, hardware debug, root-cause analysis and resolution of design issues. 
 The role requires strong hands-on knowledge of processor-based digital hardware design and the ability to independently review and debug complex customer boards. 
 The engineer will also provide periodic technical training to customers and proactively support customer design-review, board-debug and technical-support requests to help accelerate successful product development.
 Key Responsibilities: 
 1.    Board-Level Digital Design and Review: Support board-level digital hardware design and conduct detailed design reviews for customer products based on Intel Core and Atom processors. 
 2.    Schematic Review: Review customer schematics against Intel Platform Design Guides, reference schematics, datasheets, design checklists and other technical collateral, and identify potential design issues before PCB fabrication. 
 3.    Digital Interface Design: Review processor interfaces and associated circuitry, including DDR4/DDR5/LPDDR4/LPDDR5 memory; PCIe; USB; SATA; DisplayPort/eDP/HDMI and other display interfaces; Ethernet and connectivity interfaces; I2C/SMBus, SPI, UART and GPIO; and clock, reset, boot/configuration straps and other platform control signals. 
 4.    PCB Layout Review: Review multilayer PCB stack-up and board layout implementation for processor-based platforms, including controlled impedance, high-speed routing, length matching, differential-pair routing, reference planes, via structures and signal-return paths for compliance with Intel layout guidelines and industry best practices. 
 5.    High-Speed Digital Design: Perform detailed schematic and layout reviews of high-speed digital interfaces, particularly DDR, PCIe and USB, and recommend corrective actions based on Intel design guidelines and sound high-speed digital design practices. 
 6.    Component Selection and Implementation: Support selection and design implementation of board-level digital components including memory devices, clock devices, level translators, buffers, multiplexers, switches, retimers, interface controllers and supporting logic. 
 7.    Board Bring-Up and Debug: Drive and support customer board bring-up, including initial power-on, processor initialization, boot failures, memory initialization issues, high-speed interface failures and other board-level hardware issues. 
 8.    Hands-On Lab Debug: Use lab debug equipment such as oscilloscopes, digital multimeters, logic analyzers, protocol analyzers, I2C/SMBus tools and programmers to isolate and resolve hardware issues. 
 9.    Root-Cause Analysis: Analyze hardware debug data to identify root causes, differentiate between schematic, PCB-layout, component, assembly, manufacturing and configuration-related issues, and recommend corrective actions. 
 10.  Customer Issue Resolution: Actively support and drive resolution of customer technical issues, design-review requests and board-debug requests on an ongoing and periodic basis, working with customers from problem definition through root-cause identification and closure. 
 11.  Customer Technical Training: Develop and deliver periodic technical training sessions and workshops for customer engineering teams covering Intel processor-based board design, hardware design guidelines, high-speed interfaces, schematic/layout best practices, board bring-up and debug methodologies. 
 12.  Customer Hardware Enabling: Provide hands-on technical guidance to customer hardware engineers during schematic design, PCB development, prototype bring-up, EVT/DVT and initial product-enabling phases. 
 13.  Cross-Functional Issue Resolution: Collaborate with Intel silicon, platform, validation, BIOS/Firmware and other engineering teams when customer hardware issues require cross-functional investigation and resolution. 
 14.  Technical Communication: Effectively communicate design-review findings, technical risks, debug results and recommended corrective actions to customer and internal engineering teams. 
 15.  Design Best Practices: Develop and maintain hardware design-review checklists, debug procedures, technical training materials, design best practices and lessons learned for reuse across customer programs. 
 16. Customer Engagement: Periodically engage with customer engineering teams to review active designs, understand technical issues and provide timely engineering support throughout their product-development lifecycle.  
 Qualifications: Required Qualifications: 
 Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electronics/Electrical Engineering or a related discipline, with 8 to 12 years of relevant industry experience, preferably including substantial hands-on experience in processor-based board design and debug. 
 Strong hands-on experience designing and debugging complex multilayer digital boards, preferably using Intel Core/Atom or similar high-performance processor/SoC platforms. 
 Experience in schematic capture and review using industry-standard EDA tools such as Cadence OrCAD/Allegro, Siemens/Mentor Graphics Xpedition or equivalent. 
 Strong experience in processor-based schematic design/review, including CPU/SoC interfaces, DDR memory, PCIe, USB, SATA, display interfaces, Ethernet/connectivity, clock/reset, SPI/I2C/SMBus/UART/GPIO, and boot and configuration circuitry.

 Join an inclusive team passionate about one thing: using their expertise in the relentless pursuit of innovation for customers and partners. The solutions we build help make everything from artificial intelligence to advanced memory technologies possible. We do it all while committing to integrity, innovation, collaboration, and operational excellence. Because doing so fuels the next generation of semiconductor technology. 
 Job Description 
 As a Global Quality Front-End Central Quality Assurance Remote Operation Control (GQ FECTQA ROC) Engineer at Micron Technology, Inc., you will be part of a global organization responsible for centralized quality operations supporting Micron wafer fabrication sites across Asia and the United States. You will play a critical role in safeguarding product quality through automated quality screening, lot disposition, statistical risk assessment, and operational excellence initiatives. 
 In this role, you will leverage advanced statistical analysis, semiconductor process knowledge, automation, and data-driven decision-making to identify quality and reliability risks, recommend appropriate product dispositions, and drive network-wide quality improvements. You will collaborate closely with Site QA, Product Engineering, Reliability, Manufacturing, and Global Quality teams to ensure consistent execution of quality control strategies and defect containment actions across the Micron network. 
 You Will: 
 Design and Develop Quality Screening and Disposition Systems 
 Develop quality screening strategies, business rules, and disposition plans for deployment in Micron's centralized quality systems. 
 Configure and maintain automated lot hold, disposition, and containment workflows. 
 Collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders to establish risk-based quality control methodologies. 
 Support implementation and validation of quality system enhancements and screening improvements. 
 Ensure robust controls and interlocks are implemented to minimize quality escapes and operational risks. 
 Execute Wafer Lot Disposition and Quality Risk Assessment 
 Evaluate wafer lots impacted by planned or unplanned manufacturing deviations. 
 Assess quality and reliability risks using electrical test data, physical characterization results, process history, and statistical analysis. 
 Interpret outlier signals, defect signatures, and excursion indicators to determine appropriate disposition actions. 
 Support disposition activities related to Fab Conversions, Quality Deviations, Special Work Requests, and Manufacturing Excursions. 
 Document disposition decisions and provide technical justification to stakeholders. 
 Perform Advanced Data Analytics and Statistical Monitoring 
 Analyze large manufacturing datasets to identify abnormal signatures, trends, and potential quality risks. 
 Develop statistical models and methodologies for outlier detection, screening optimization, and excursion monitoring. 
 Perform distribution analysis, SPC review, baseline trending, and risk assessment activities. 
 Create dashboards, metrics, and reporting solutions to improve operational visibility and decision-making. 
 Drive data-based continuous improvement opportunities across Micron's manufacturing network. 
 Drive Automation and Digital Transformation Initiatives 
 Support AI, machine learning, and advanced analytics initiatives for quality monitoring and disposition automation. 
 Reduce manual intervention by implementing fail-safe controls, automated workflows, and decision-support systems. 
 Partner with software development teams to define requirements and deploy scalable automation solutions. 
 Continuously identify opportunities to enhance system capability and throughput. 
 Collaborate Across Global Quality Organizations 
 Partner with Site QA teams to ensure consistent quality execution across all manufacturing locations. 
 Participate in global alignment teams focused on quality standards, operational excellence, and best practice sharing. 
 Support root cause investigations and corrective/preventive action (CAPA) development. 
 Communicate technical findings, recommendations, and business impacts to diverse stakeholders. 
 Contribute to the development and publication of global quality metrics and performance indicators. 
 Support Operational Excellence and Continuous Improvement 
 Identify process gaps and propose innovative solutions to improve quality operations. 
 Lead or participate in cross-functional projects focused on productivity, quality, and automation. 
 Develop and maintain operational procedures, business process documentation, and training materials. 
 Support audits, compliance reviews, and quality system assessments. 
 Drive standardization and scalability of centralized quality operations. 
 Education 
 Required: Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Material Science, Statistics or related technical discipline. 
 Preferred: Master's Degree in Electrical or Electronics Engineering, Statistics, Data Analytics, or related field. 
 Required Qualifications 
 3–5 years of experience in Semiconductor manufacturing, product engineering, quality, reliability, test engineering, or related industry experience. 
 Strong understanding of statistical methodologies, including: Statistical Process Control (SPC) 
 Outlier Detection 
 Distribution Analysis 
 Trend Analysis 
 Data Visualization 
 Risk Assessment Methodologies 
 Knowledge of semiconductor manufacturing processes

desc:

 Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all. 
 Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.
 The Global Procurement team is an integral engine to Micron’s growth, delivering best-in-class total cost and supply chain resiliency through innovative predictive capabilities, risk analysis, and a focus on sustainability and diversity. Our business goals are directly tied to the value we place on our team members, our greatest asset. We invest in our people through a skills-based learning and development model to create clear career pathways for growth. Join us and discover why Micron’s Global Procurement team is the preferred destination to ignite your talent.
 As Senior Manager, Data Excellence & Governance within Global Procurement’s Digital Transformation & AI organization, you will lead the function that makes procurement data trusted, measurable, and ready for AI. You own data governance and quality operations, Global Procurement performance metrics and reporting, and the procurement data strategy — and you lead a multi-region team across Singapore, the United States, India, and Malaysia.
 Data readiness is the single largest constraint to unlocking value from AI, automation, and analytics in procurement. A core part of your mandate is to reimagine the data governance and excellence operating model with AI agents embedded — redefining how policies, quality monitoring, lineage, and stewardship operate when agents handle detection, enrichment, routing, and maintenance, and where people focus on exception handling, governance, and continuous improvement. Success is measured by whether prioritized workflows run on trusted, agent-consumable data, and whether the data foundation strengthens itself through automated feedback loops rather than manual clean-up.
 This is a people-leadership role. You will develop a team of data governance and analytics professionals, set the standards and stewardship model for procurement data, and partner closely with AI Transformation, Data & Process Automation, Platform Excellence, IT, Security, and Compliance to ensure the data foundation aligns with enterprise platforms, ERP readiness, and enterprise data governance standards.
 ▍ Key Responsibilities 
 A core expectation is to move procurement’s data function from reactive clean-up to an agent-embedded, self-improving operating model — where governance is executable, quality is measurable, and business value is demonstrable. 
 Data Governance & Quality Operations 
 Own the procurement data governance framework — policies, standards, decision rights, and the data stewardship operating model — and ensure it is applied consistently across systems and regions.
 Lead data quality and master data operations (Vendor Master, Material Master, spend, category taxonomy), moving from recurring manual clean-up toward monitored, controlled, and preventable quality at the source.
 Shift governance from static documents to executable rules — champion lightweight, machine-readable policies and standards that agents can enforce automatically.
 Align data handling with enterprise controls — sensitivity labels, data loss prevention, and approved access — so data can be used safely by both people and AI agents.
 Business Value & Performance Measurement 
 Own Global Procurement KPIs, metrics, and program reporting — providing leaders with a single, trusted source for performance and value.
 Lead the labor productivity and business value agenda: define, quantify, and report the value realized from transformation, automation, and AI initiatives.
 Establish data quality KPIs, service level agreements, and monitoring so quality and value are managed with evidence, not assumed.
 Procurement Data Strategy & AI Readiness 
 Reimagine the data governance and excellence operating model with agents embedded — defining the target model, the agentic patterns that apply (data quality agent, lineage agent, maintenance agent, steward copilot), and a getting-started roadmap sequenced against ERP and transformation milestones.
 Set and drive the procurement data strategy, prioritizing the Critical Data Elements that carry the most downstream value.
 Partner with the AI Data Strategist and agent build leads to define the data elements, quality thresholds, and validation rules each agent needs — mapping every business requirement to a source, owner, and readiness action.
 Direct the design of the feedback loop between agent, source system, and steward so validation, correction, and prevention happen without manual clean-up wherever feasible.
 Data Lineage & Technical Foundations 
 Direct the working-level technical foundations that make the agentic model possible — data lineage, relationships, schema, and cross-system mapping — so downstream impact is traceable before a change lands.
 Stand up and maintain a searchable data dictionary, business glossary, documentation, versioning, and change history that both people and agents can query and update.
 Define control points at the point of entry so quality is protected where data originates.
 Innovation & Reusable Assets 
 Sponsor rapid experiments on agentic data patterns, validate impact, and turn the best into reusable building blocks for broader adoption across Source-to-Pay.
 Pilot AI-based data validation and cleansing tools and assess fit against Micron’s data landscape.
 Team Leadership, Enterprise Partnership & Change 
 Lead, coach, and develop a multi-region team; build depth, ownership

 Global Quality Front-End Central Quality Assurance Engineer/Sr Engineer  – (GQ FECTQA MOI) 
 Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all. 
 Join an inclusive team passionate about one thing: using their expertise in the relentless pursuit of innovation for customers and partners. The solutions we build help make everything from artificial intelligence to advanced memory technologies possible. We do it all while committing to integrity, innovation, collaboration, and operational excellence. Because doing so fuels the next generation of semiconductor technology. 
 Job Description 
 As a Global Quality Front-End Central Quality Assurance Remote Operation Control (GQ FECTQA ROC) Engineer at Micron Technology, Inc., you will be part of a global organization responsible for centralized quality operations supporting Micron wafer fabrication sites across Asia and the United States. You will play a critical role in safeguarding product quality through automated quality screening, lot disposition, statistical risk assessment, and operational excellence initiatives. 
 In this role, you will leverage advanced statistical analysis, semiconductor process knowledge, automation, and data-driven decision-making to identify quality and reliability risks, recommend appropriate product dispositions, and drive network-wide quality improvements. You will collaborate closely with Site QA, Product Engineering, Reliability, Manufacturing, and Global Quality teams to ensure consistent execution of quality control strategies and defect containment actions across the Micron network. 
 You Will: 
 Design and Develop Quality Screening and Disposition Systems 
 Develop quality screening strategies, business rules, and disposition plans for deployment in Micron's centralized quality systems. 
 Configure and maintain automated lot hold, disposition, and containment workflows. 
 Collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders to establish risk-based quality control methodologies. 
 Support implementation and validation of quality system enhancements and screening improvements. 
 Ensure robust controls and interlocks are implemented to minimize quality escapes and operational risks. 
 Execute Wafer Lot Disposition and Quality Risk Assessment 
 Evaluate wafer lots impacted by planned or unplanned manufacturing deviations. 
 Assess quality and reliability risks using electrical test data, physical characterization results, process history, and statistical analysis. 
 Interpret outlier signals, defect signatures, and excursion indicators to determine appropriate disposition actions. 
 Support disposition activities related to Fab Conversions, Quality Deviations, Special Work Requests, and Manufacturing Excursions. 
 Document disposition decisions and provide technical justification to stakeholders. 
 Perform Advanced Data Analytics and Statistical Monitoring 
 Analyze large manufacturing datasets to identify abnormal signatures, trends, and potential quality risks. 
 Develop statistical models and methodologies for outlier detection, screening optimization, and excursion monitoring. 
 Perform distribution analysis, SPC review, baseline trending, and risk assessment activities. 
 Create dashboards, metrics, and reporting solutions to improve operational visibility and decision-making. 
 Drive data-based continuous improvement opportunities across Micron's manufacturing network. 
 Drive Automation and Digital Transformation Initiatives 
 Support AI, machine learning, and advanced analytics initiatives for quality monitoring and disposition automation. 
 Reduce manual intervention by implementing fail-safe controls, automated workflows, and decision-support systems. 
 Partner with software development teams to define requirements and deploy scalable automation solutions. 
 Continuously identify opportunities to enhance system capability and throughput. 
 Collaborate Across Global Quality Organizations 
 Partner with Site QA teams to ensure consistent quality execution across all manufacturing locations. 
 Participate in global alignment teams focused on quality standards, operational excellence, and best practice sharing. 
 Support root cause investigations and corrective/preventive action (CAPA) development. 
 Communicate technical findings, recommendations, and business impacts to diverse stakeholders. 
 Contribute to the development and publication of global quality metrics and performance indicators. 
 Support Operational Excellence and Continuous Improvement 
 Identify process gaps and propose innovative solutions to improve quality operations. 
 Lead or participate in cross-functional projects focused on productivity, quality, and automation. 
 Develop and maintain operational procedures, business process documentation, and training materials. 
 Support audits, compliance reviews, and quality system assessments. 
 Drive standardization and scalability of centralized quality operations. 
 Education 
 Required: Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Material Science, Statistics or related technical discipline. 
 Preferred: Master's Degree in Electrical or Electronics Engineering, Statistics, Data Analytics, or related field. 
 Required Qualifications 
 3–5 years of experience in Semiconductor manufacturing, product engineering, quality, reliability, test engineering, or related industry experience. 
 Strong understanding of statistical methodologies, including: Statistical Process Control (SPC) 
 Outlier Detection 
 Distribution Analysis 
 Trend Analysis 
 Data Visualization 
 Risk Assessment Methodologies 
 Knowledge of semiconductor manufacturing processes

desc:

 In the Technology Development — Advanced Modeling & AI Solutions (AMAIS) organization, you will be part of a multidisciplinary team developing next-generation Digital Twins, predictive modeling solutions, and AI-driven technologies that accelerate advanced memory development and manufacturing excellence.  You will create predictive digital representations of semiconductor processes, materials, structures, equipment, and products across DRAM, NAND, and advanced packaging technologies including HBM.  Leveraging physics-based modeling, computational methods, machine learning, GenAI, large language models (LLMs), and agentic AI frameworks, you will enable technology co-optimization, design-space exploration, process optimization, yield improvement, and accelerated technology learning.  Working at the intersection of engineering fundamentals, manufacturing data, and digital engineering, you will develop scalable predictive and prescriptive solutions that connect process, structure, performance, yield, reliability, and cost.  This role offers the opportunity to influence critical technology decisions, drive  fab-technology co-optimization , and advance Micron's leadership in data-driven semiconductor memory innovation.
 Qualifications: 
 Independence – be comfortable executing activities and needs
 Experience in algorithm development, numerical methods, and scientific computing
 Solid experience with Plasma, FPM, HAR etching, and MC modeling
 Experience with Wet Processes, Chemical Etching and Strip, Material selectivity, Chemistry evaluation, etc.
 Strong background in thermodynamics, physics, and chemistry
 Experience with computational materials science methodologies
 Familiar with machine learning and deep learning concepts and applications
 Experience with regression, neural networks, and frameworks
 Familiar with process and multi-physics modeling, and implementation
 Experience with common modeling software, previous software development and Linux experience
 Experience with Bash, Python, FORTRAN, or C++
 Experience with OpenFOAM, ANSYS Fluent, COMSOL, HPEM
 Strong debug and problem-solving skills
 Experience writing reports and conference papers
 Excellent written and verbal communication
 Ability to work in a team environment and experience with remote collaboration tools
   Responsibilities 
 Develop and deploy Digital Twins and predictive models spanning process, wafer, die, package, and manufacturing domains to enable technology and fab co-optimization.
 Develop structural and Multiphysics models to evaluate process-structure-performance interactions, including stress, deformation, cracking, voiding, and reliability risks.
 Build physics-informed composite AI models that accelerate technology development, yield improvement, reliability assessment, and design-space exploration.
 Apply advanced computational methods, machine learning, and sparse-data modeling techniques to create robust predictive and prescriptive solutions for complex semiconductor challenges.
 Utilize state-of-the-art GenAI, LLM-powered copilots, RAG systems, and agentic AI workflows that integrate engineering tools, knowledge bases, simulation environments, and manufacturing data.
 Collaborate across global engineering teams to translate modeling insights into actionable technology decisions.

 Support   AWS Bedrock ,   Bedrock Studio ,   Amazon Q Business ,   Bedrock Knowledge Bases ,   Guardrails , and   Bedrock   AgentCore .

 Ensure secure and compliant deployment of AI services, APIs, agents, and applications.   
 4. Cloud Operations and Optimization

 Manage and   optimize   cloud resources including   compute , storage, networking, databases, containers, and AI services.

 7 . Observability, Reliability and Support

title: Senior Data Scientist– Pricing
location: Bengaluru, Karnataka, India; Tlaquepaque, Jalisco, Mexico
desc:
Senior Data Scientist– Pricing 
 Description - 
 About the role 
 HP's B2B Pricing Data Science team builds the analytics and ML systems that set and negotiate prices for commercial PC and Print products, sold both through channel partners and directly to business customers worldwide. Our pricing engine combines machine learning price and win-rate models, causal price elasticity estimation, and constrained optimization, and is deployed in live A/B pilots across multiple markets. We are expanding the team's global footprint to better support a global product.
 You will work at the intersection of econometrics and production data science: improving the causal inference core of our pricing algorithm, designing experiments to measure the impact of pricing and process interventions, and shipping your work as production-quality Python code. You will report directly to the team's manager, partner closely with our senior applied data scientist on methodology, and operate with a high degree of autonomy.
 What you will do 
 Advance the causal inference components of our pricing system: price elasticity estimation (double/debiased ML, heterogeneous treatment effects), uncertainty quantification, and optimization logic.
 Design, run, and analyze experiments and quasi-experiments (A/B tests, diff-in-diff, synthetic control) to measure the impact of pricing and process interventions, including where clean randomization isn't possible.
 Translate methodological improvements into production-ready Python code, with tests, documentation, and adherence to team engineering standards.
 Contribute to the operational health of our production systems: incident support, model monitoring, and periodic retraining and validation cycles.
 Communicate findings and recommendations to technical and business stakeholders across time zones.
 What you bring 
 4–5+ years of professional experience in data science, econometrics, or quantitative research, ideally with exposure to pricing, revenue management, or marketplaces.
 Strong grounding in causal inference and experimental design: potential outcomes framework, DML/orthogonalization, CATE estimation, instrumental variables, panel methods.
 Solid applied ML skills (gradient boosting, regularized regression) and the statistical judgment to know when a predictive model answers a causal question — and when it doesn't.
 Proficient Python for production: clean, testable, maintainable code; comfortable with the scikit-learn ecosystem, Git-based workflows, and code review.
 Hands-on experience with Databricks (or comparable cloud data platforms) for development and deployment.
 Proactive, self-directed working style: you reach out early when blocked, over-communicate in a distributed team, and don't wait for co-location to collaborate.
 Fluent English; comfortable working with predominantly CET-based colleagues.
 Nice to have 
 Experience with EconML, DoWhy, or similar causal ML libraries; conformal prediction.
 Effective use of GenAI tools for coding and research — our team works extensively with AI coding assistants (e.g., Codex, GitHub Copilot) as part of daily development.
 B2B pricing domain knowledge (quotes, deal negotiation, discounting, channel dynamics).
 Advanced degree (MSc/PhD) in economics, statistics, or a quantitative field.
 Education 
 Full time Master's degree, PhD/Doctorate will be added advantage (not mandatory)

title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer
location: Bengaluru, Karnataka, India; Tlaquepaque, Jalisco, Mexico
desc:
Senior Machine Learning Engineer 
 Description - 
 We are looking for a Senior MLOps Engineer to design, build, and operate the infrastructure that enables machine learning models and large language models to be deployed safely, reliably, and at scale.
 In this role, you will create the end-to-end capabilities required to move models from experimentation into production, expose them through secure and highly available endpoints, and enable users and applications to interact with AI-powered services.
 You will work across AWS and Databricks to establish robust CI/CD pipelines, model-serving infrastructure, observability, governance, rollback mechanisms, and operational standards. You will partner closely with data scientists, machine learning engineers, software engineers, security teams, and platform engineers.
 The ideal candidate combines strong cloud and DevOps engineering skills with a practical understanding of machine learning systems, LLM deployment patterns, and production reliability.
 Key Responsibilities
 MLOps Platform and Architecture
 Design and implement a scalable MLOps platform using AWS and Databricks.
 Define reference architectures and reusable deployment patterns for traditional machine learning models, deep learning models, and large language models.
 Build standardized workflows that move models from development and validation into staging and production.
 Develop self-service capabilities that allow data scientists and ML engineers to deploy models without manually managing infrastructure.
 Establish clear separation between development, testing, staging, and production environments.
 Design multi-region or multi-availability-zone architectures where required by business continuity and availability objectives.
 CI/CD and Model Deployment
 Build automated CI/CD pipelines for model code, inference services, infrastructure, configuration, and model artifacts.
 Implement automated testing across the deployment lifecycle, including:
 Unit testing
 Integration testing
 Model validation
 Data contract validation
 API and endpoint testing
 Security testing
 Performance and load testing
 Regression testing
 Automate model packaging, containerization, versioning, approval, promotion, and deployment.
 Support deployment strategies such as blue-green deployments, canary releases, shadow deployments, and controlled traffic shifting.
 Implement reliable rollback and roll-forward mechanisms for application code, infrastructure, model versions, prompts, and configuration.
 Ensure deployments are reproducible, auditable, and recoverable.
 Model and LLM Serving
 Design and operate secure, scalable, low-latency inference endpoints.
 Deploy models using appropriate services and patterns across AWS and Databricks, such as:
 Databricks Model Serving
 MLflow Model Registry
 Amazon SageMaker
 Amazon ECS or EKS
 AWS Lambda, where appropriate
 API Gateway
 Application Load Balancers
 Build synchronous, asynchronous, batch, and streaming inference capabilities.
 Design serving architectures for LLM-powered applications, including:
 Hosted foundation models
 Open-source models
 Fine-tuned models
 Retrieval-augmented generation
 Embedding services
 Vector search
 Prompt and response orchestration
 Tool-calling and agentic workflows
 Optimize inference performance, scalability, GPU utilization, concurrency, throughput, latency, and cost.
 Implement autoscaling, request throttling, queuing, caching, timeout handling, and graceful degradation.
 Reliability, Recovery, and Business Continuity
 Build recoverable model-serving endpoints with clearly defined recovery time and recovery point objectives.
 Implement automated health checks, failover mechanisms, retry policies, circuit breakers, and service recovery procedures.
 Design backup and recovery processes for:
 Model artifacts
 Model registry metadata
 Feature definitions
 Deployment configurations
 Infrastructure state
 Prompts and application configuration
 Vector indexes and knowledge-base assets
 Create disaster recovery procedures and regularly test restoration and failover capabilities.
 Ensure production services can recover from failed deployments, infrastructure outages, model errors, and upstream dependency failures.
 Develop operational runbooks and incident response procedures.
 Monitoring and Observability
 Implement end-to-end observability for infrastructure, applications, models, data, and user interactions.
 Monitor:
 Availability
 Request volume
 Latency
 Error rates
 Resource utilization
 Model performance
 Data quality
 Data drift
 Concept drift
 Prediction distributions
 LLM response quality
 Hallucination and safety indicators
 Token consumption
 Cost per request
 Establish dashboards, alerts, service-level indicators, and service-level objectives.
 Integrate monitoring with incident management and on-call processes.
 Enable traceability from user requests through model inference, retrieval, orchestration, and downstream services.
 Support root-cause analysis by maintaining structured logs, metrics, traces, model lineage, and deployment history.
 Security and Governance
 Implement security controls for model-serving environments, APIs, data access, and deployment pipelines.
 Apply least-privilege access using AWS IAM, Databricks permissions, service principals, and role-based access control.
 Secure secrets, credentials, API keys, certificates, and tokens using approved secrets-management solutions.
 Implement encryption in transit and at rest.
 Design private networking, endpoint controls, firewall rules, and secure connectivity patterns.
 Support authentication, authorization, rate limiting, and tenant isolation for AI services.
 Ensure models and LLM applications comply with organizational requirements for privacy, security, auditability, and responsible AI.
 Maintain model lineage, approval records, version history, and deployment audit trails.
 Implement controls for sensitive data, personally identifiable information

 We are looking for a hands-on Data Scientist to strengthen our analytics pipelines that support planning, forecasting, and inventory optimization across the HP supply chain network. Demonstrated ability to build regression, classification, or time-series models for business applications. Familiarity with feature engineering techniques such as lag, rolling, and categorical encoding, and awareness of methods to prevent data leakage. Experience with workflow automation, reproducibility, and parameterized scripts. Ability to explain analytical results and model behavior in business terms.

title: Enterprise Technology Costing Architect
location: Spring, Texas, United States of America; Bengaluru, Karnataka, India
desc:
Enterprise Technology Costing Architect 
 Description - 
 Job Summary 
The Enterprise Technology Costing Architect owns the end-to-end enterprise technology architecture for Costing , translating the approved Costing business solution blueprint into an integrated, scalable, secure and sustainable technology architecture across applications, data, integration, platforms and downstream systems.
 The role ensures that technology decisions across SAP S/4HANA, SAP PaPM, data platforms, integration technologies, analytics and downstream solutions operate as one coherent enterprise architecture rather than a collection of locally optimized solutions.
 The architect protects architectural coherence, enterprise standards, reuse, scalability and long-term technology sustainability , while providing architecture assurance from solution design through implementation, deployment and transition to run.
 The role works in close partnership with the Costing Business Solution Architect , Enterprise Architecture, Digital teams, solution/platform architects, technology owners and implementation partners.
 Key Responsibilities 
 1. Enterprise Costing Technology Architecture 
 Own and maintain the E2E target technology architecture and technology roadmap for Costing .
 Translate the approved business solution blueprint and required business capabilities into the target technology architecture.
 Define how applications, platforms, data, integrations and downstream systems work together as one enterprise costing technology ecosystem .
 Ensure alignment with enterprise architecture principles, security requirements and technology standards.
 Lead architecture reviews and technology design decisions that materially affect the E2E Costing architecture.
 2. Application & Platform Architecture 
 Own the target application/system architecture across the Costing technology landscape.
 Determine how approved Costing capabilities should be enabled across SAP S/4HANA, SAP PaPM, analytics, data platforms, integration platforms and supporting/downstream applications .
 Drive architectural reuse and rationalization, avoiding unnecessary duplication or technology fragmentation.
 Evaluate technology options based on architectural fit, scalability, maintainability, reuse and enterprise sustainability.
 Assess emerging technologies, including AI and automation, where they can enable the approved Costing business solution.
 3. Data & Integration Architecture 
 Own the architecture for costing data movement, storage, integration and consumption .
 Define E2E integration architecture, interface patterns and technology dependencies across ERP, Supply Chain, Product, Finance, data platforms and downstream systems.
 Ensure architectural support for required data quality, traceability, reconciliation and auditability.
 Partner with business/data owners to ensure the technology architecture supports defined business information requirements and semantics.
 4. Architecture Governance & Design Assurance 
 Establish and apply architecture principles, standards, patterns and technology guardrails for Costing.
 Ensure solution designs comply with the approved enterprise technology architecture.
 Lead/challenge decisions that alter the Costing technology architecture, integration model, platform strategy or technical standards .
 Manage architectural risks, technical debt and architecture exceptions.
 Provide architecture assurance throughout detailed design, build, testing, deployment and transition to run.
 5. Cross-Technology Coherence 
 Prevent individual technology decisions across SAP, PaPM, data, integration, reporting and downstream systems from creating fragmented architecture.
 Identify cross-system dependencies and architectural impacts early in solution design.
 Ensure individual solution/platform designs collectively deliver the approved E2E business solution.
 Work with Enterprise Architecture and relevant technology owners to resolve cross-domain architecture decisions.
 6. Transformation & Vendor Architecture Leadership 
 Provide E2E technology architecture leadership throughout the Costing Transformation.
 Challenge implementation partner and vendor designs against the approved business solution, enterprise architecture and long-term technology strategy.
 Evaluate alternative solution options and innovations proposed by partners based on technical feasibility, architectural fit, enterprise reuse, scalability and sustainability .
 Ensure the company retains long-term architectural ownership rather than allowing architecture to become vendor defined.
 Maintain technical continuity from architecture → detailed solution design → build → deployment → run .

 TOGAF® Enterprise Architecture Practitioner 
 Open Certified Architect (Open CA) (highly desirable for distinguished technologist level)
 SAP Architecture & Costing Platforms

 Data & Integration Architecture

 Integration Architecture / API Management Certifications (MuleSoft, SAP Integration Suite, Azure Integration Services)
 AI & Emerging Technologies
 Microsoft Certified: Azure AI Engineer Associate 
 AI Architecture or Generative AI Certifications relevant to enterprise AI enablement
 Cross-Org Skills 
 • Effective Communication
 • Results Orientation
 • Learning Agility
 • Digital Fluency
 • Customer Centricity
 Impact & Scope 
 • Impacts multiple functions and influences long-term strategic direction across multiple disciplines or areas of HP.

title: Interaction and Motion designer
desc:
Interaction and Motion designer 
 Description - 
 About the Role We're building the operating system for a next-generation device, and we're looking for a talented Interaction Designer to shape how it feels to use .
 This role is centered around interaction design and motion — the details that make an interface feel alive, responsive, intuitive, and delightful. You'll define how the OS behaves at a moment-to-moment level: how things move, respond, transition, provide feedback, and communicate state.
 Your primary focus will be bringing craft, consistency, and delight to the experience across the OS. You'll help define the interaction language of the product and ensure that interactions feel cohesive rather than a collection of individual features.
 Alongside this, you'll contribute to selected UX and UI projects with the broader design team, either independently or in collaboration with other designers.
 What You'll Do Define what "delight" means for the product and translate it into thoughtful, purposeful interactions across the OS.
 Own the interaction design and micro-animation layer of the OS, including transitions, spatial relationships, feedback, gestures, states, loading, success/error, sound, haptics and other moment-to-moment behaviors.
 Collaborate with product designers, product managers, engineers, and other stakeholders to brainstorm and develop interaction concepts for the device.
 Define and maintain a consistent interaction language so that behaviors across the OS feel unified and intentional, across different modal behaviors like touch, trackpad, keyboard and stylus.
 Build, maintain, and evolve an interaction library covering reusable patterns, behaviors, motion principles, timing, and transitions.
 Contribute to the broader design system and work with other designers to ensure interaction patterns are documented, consistent, and reusable.
 Prototype interactions using tools such as Figma, Principle, ProtoPie, After Effects, or code-based prototyping.
 Use prototypes to communicate not just visual behavior, but also motion, timing, sound, feedback, and overall feel.
 Partner closely with engineering throughout implementation to ensure interactions are brought to life with a high level of design fidelity.
 Review builds, identify interaction or motion inconsistencies, and work with engineers to refine the experience while taking feasibility and performance into account.
 Explore emerging interaction patterns, motion techniques, and interaction paradigms across leading products globally, bringing relevant ideas and inspiration into the product.
 Contribute to UX and UI projects across the product team, either independently owning selected projects or supporting other UX designers with interaction design and prototyping.
 What We're Looking For 
 A portfolio that clearly demonstrates strong interaction design and motion/micro-animation craft. This is the most important qualification for this role. 
 The ability to take ownership of interactions across an OS and drive them from concept through implementation with engineering.
 Strong prototyping skills — you're comfortable communicating interactions through working prototypes rather than static screens alone.
 An understanding of motion as a tool for usability, hierarchy, feedback, continuity, and delight — not simply as visual decoration.
 Strong design judgment and restraint: knowing when motion adds value and when simplicity is the better experience.
 Working knowledge of design systems and how interaction patterns can be made consistent, reusable, and scalable.
 Comfort working across both craft-heavy interaction design and broader product design work.
 Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to articulate design decisions to product managers, designers, engineers, and leadership.
 The ability to work directly with engineers on implementation details and advocate for interaction quality and design fidelity.
 Experience working with sound or other forms of sensory feedback as part of interaction design.
 Nice to Have Experience designing for an OS-level, system-level, or gaming platform , rather than only individual applications.
 Experience with tablet, mobile, or multi-modal interaction design involving combinations of touch, keyboard, pen, or other input methods.
 Familiarity with the performance considerations of animation on devices, including frame rates, GPU constraints, and how these influence interaction design decisions.
 A background in motion design, game UI, or consumer products with rich micro-interactions.
 Education & Experience Recommended 
• Four-year or Graduate Degree in Design, Human Factors Engineering, Social Sciences research, or any other related discipline or commensurate work experience or demonstrated competence.
 Around 5 years of experience across UI, UX, and, most importantly, interaction design.

As a Mechanical Engineer, you’ll leverage your strong foundation in physics, mathematics, and materials science to process and resolve mechanical problems, design and implement custom mechanical tooling and associated processes, and enable the handling, assembly, and disassembly of parts, components, sub-assemblies, and final assemblies throughout the product life cycle. You'll be responsible for designing, developing, and modifying mechanical engineering layouts, schematics, and specifications. You will oversee manufacturing and installation processes, ensuring adherence to industry standards and regulations-- and you'll coordinate the procurement and assembly of mechanical components and equipment for design projects, identifying sources of critical parts and subsystems to resolve technical issues.  
 Key Responsibilities Own the full design lifecycle of mechanical assemblies: concept, feasibility, detailed design, prototype, test, qualification and release to manufacturing.
 Design precision mechanisms such as lens and mirror mounts, kinematic mounts, flexures, alignment stages and optical benches.
 Do engineering calculations and analysis, including tolerance stack-ups, stress and deflection, thermal expansion, stiffness, vibration and natural frequency.
 Run FEA (structural, thermal, modal) to validate designs and guide trade-offs.
 Apply GD&T (ASME Y14.5) and create complete 3D models, detailed drawings and BOMs.
 Write test plans and qualification protocols, run testing, analyze data and drive root cause and corrective actions.
 Lead design reviews (PDR/CDR) and maintain design documentation, DFMEA and design verification reports.
 Apply DFM/DFA principles and work with suppliers on manufacturability, cost and lead time.
 Deliver work on schedule and to quality and cost targets, and communicate status and risks clearly.
 Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering (Master’s preferred).
 5+ years of mechanical design experience.
 Strong SPM (Special Purpose Machine) design background, from concept to detailed design.
 Strong engineering fundamentals and calculation skills: mechanics, strength of materials, machine design, heat transfer.
 Proficiency in 3D CAD and PLM tools.
 Working knowledge of FEA tools (ANSYS or equivalent).
 Sound knowledge of GD&T, tolerance analysis, materials and manufacturing processes (machining, sheet metal, surface treatments).
 Proven ownership of design testing and qualification.
 Preferred Qualifications Experience in semiconductor capital equipment, metrology, inspection or optical systems.
 Knowledge of optical alignment, opto-mechanical tolerancing and thermal/vibration stability.
 Exposure to cleanroom and vacuum compatible design and materials.
 Familiarity with motion systems, precision stages and actuators.
 Experience with DFMEA, DOE and statistical data analysis.
 Behavioral Competencies Professionalism: high integrity, accountable and dependable.
 Commitment to delivery: consistently meets schedules and quality targets.
 Ownership: takes full responsibility for subsystem outcomes.
