title: Senior Software Engineer, AI Framework Integrations
desc:
AI frameworks like LangChain, LlamaIndex, and n8n are quickly becoming the default way developers build with AI — and MongoDB wants to be the data platform that shows up everywhere they build. As part of the AI Builders Experience (ABX) org, we're standing up a brand new engineering team in Gurugram to make that happen, and we're looking for Senior Software Engineers to be among its founding members.
 The team owns the connective layer between MongoDB and third-party AI frameworks, platforms, and tools — the integrations that let developers use MongoDB effectively with the AI stack they've already chosen. That means shipping into some of the fastest-moving open-source ecosystems in tech, working mostly in Python and TypeScript, and partnering with the Database Experience (DBX) org when an integration needs new driver, platform, or product capability underneath it.
 This is a self-sufficient team by design. You and your engineering manager will be based in Gurugram, and the group is set up to own its area end to end: to decide how integrations get built, tested, released, and maintained, without waiting on another time zone to unblock the day-to-day. You'll work closest with the engineers sitting next to you, pairing on hard problems, reviewing each other's code, and dividing up a broad portfolio, while collaborating with product, partners, field teams, and open source maintainers as the work requires.
 You'll integrate with fast-moving, often unproven technologies, make pragmatic calls in the face of ambiguity, and own high-visibility projects with minimal guidance. Priorities can shift week to week based on framework changes, customer demand, and partner needs, so we're looking for product-minded engineers who thrive on autonomy and take pride in shipping. Much of your work will happen in public: sending pull requests to upstream repositories, working through external maintainer review cycles, and representing MongoDB in developer communities.
 MongoDB engineering teams pride themselves on building high-quality software and living our cultural values every day — we value intellectual curiosity, intellectual honesty, customer empathy, and building together in an environment that prioritizes collaboration over competition.
 We are looking to speak to candidates who are based in Gurugram for our hybrid working model.
 Position expectations 
 Design, build, test, and ship MongoDB integrations across a broad AI framework ecosystem that includes technologies like LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, n8n, and Mastra, owning them from first exploratory spike through production release and ongoing maintenance.
 Take ownership of ambiguous problems and drive them to completion independently, making sound decisions as requirements, frameworks, and customer needs evolve.
 Do the initial, exploratory work: assess a new framework, define the smallest useful version of an integration, get it in front of users quickly, and make a clear recommendation about whether and how to invest further.
 Contribute high-quality code upstream to repositories MongoDB doesn't own, maintaining a high standard of professionalism and courtesy while working through external maintainer review cycles.
 Build and maintain the team's engineering practices for a broad integration portfolio, including CI/CD, automated testing across framework and server versions, version compatibility awareness, and release readiness.
 Own the operational health of the integrations you build — monitoring, upgrades, breaking-change response, issue triage, and follow-through after launch.
 Partner with the Database Experience (DBX) org to define the driver, platform, and product capabilities your integrations depend on, making the case for what's needed and why.
 Work with product management, product design, partners, field teams, and open source maintainers to define the first version and future evolution of these integrations.
 Raise the technical bar within the team: shape architecture and development practices, give thorough code reviews, share what you know, and mentor peers and less experienced engineers.
 Stay current with the Python, TypeScript, and broader AI builder ecosystems and bring what you learn back to the team's roadmap.
 Bring a research and discovery mindset: notice emerging opportunities in the ecosystem, surface them early, and make the case for where MongoDB should show up next.
 Flag issues, risks, and resource needs early and clearly, both within the team and to cross-functional partners in other regions.
 Qualifications 
 Strong background in building core components for scalable, high-availability services, developer platforms, or libraries
 7+ years of experience building backend systems or developer-facing libraries, with strong proficiency in Python and/or TypeScript
 Proven success in designing, writing, testing, debugging, and performance tuning software in large, long-lived code bases, including code that other developers depend on
 Track record of identifying problems, implementing solutions, and delivering complex projects independently with minimal guidance
 A product-minded approach to engineering, with the judgment to make pragmatic tradeoffs between fast time-to-market and long-term maintainability, and the comfort to operate amid ambiguity and rapidly evolving technologies

 Strong and demonstrated interest in modern AI builder workflows and the developer tooling landscape: AI frameworks, agentic patterns, RAG and retrieval, embedding, vector search, or adjacent areas.

title: Software Engineer 3, AI Framework Integrations
desc:
AI frameworks like LangChain, LlamaIndex, and n8n are quickly becoming the default way developers build with AI — and MongoDB wants to be the data platform that shows up everywhere they build. As part of the AI Builders Experience (ABX) org, we're standing up a brand new engineering team in Gurugram to make that happen, and we're looking for Software Engineers to be among its founding members.
 The team owns the connective layer between MongoDB and third-party AI frameworks, platforms, and tools — the integrations that let developers use MongoDB effectively with the AI stack they've already chosen. That means shipping into some of the fastest-moving open-source ecosystems in tech, working mostly in Python and TypeScript, and partnering with the Database Experience (DBX) org when an integration needs new driver, platform, or product capability underneath it.
 This is a strong role for an engineer who wants to grow into the AI space with real ownership. You'll own well-scoped projects from design through release, work with fast-moving and sometimes unproven technologies, and get a clear view of how the ecosystem is evolving. Priorities shift as frameworks change and customer demand moves, so we're looking for engineers who are adaptable, ask good questions, and take pride in shipping. Much of your work will happen in public: sending pull requests to upstream repositories, working through external maintainer review cycles, and participating in developer communities as MongoDB.
 You'll work closest with the engineers sitting next to you, pairing on hard problems, reviewing each other's code, and dividing up a broad portfolio, with senior engineers and your manager close at hand as you take on larger pieces of it.
 MongoDB engineering teams pride themselves on building high-quality software and living our cultural values every day. We value intellectual curiosity, intellectual honesty, customer empathy, and building together in an environment that prioritizes collaboration over competition.
 We are looking to speak to candidates who are based in Gurugram for our hybrid working model.
 Position expectations 
 Build, test, and ship MongoDB integrations across a broad AI framework ecosystem that includes technologies like LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, n8n, and Mastra
 Own well-scoped projects end to end on weekly-to-quarterly timelines, taking responsibility for the scope, schedule, and quality of your own work and communicating progress and trade-offs clearly
 Solve day-to-day technical problems with growing independence, using the team's established patterns and past practice to guide your decisions, and seeking guidance on non-standard problems
 Contribute to exploratory work on new frameworks: help evaluate an integration's feasibility, build a first working version of the piece you own, and share what you learn with the team
 Contribute high-quality code upstream to repositories MongoDB doesn't own, following the team's contribution practices and maintaining a high standard of professionalism and courtesy through external maintainer review cycles
 Work within and improve the team's engineering practices: CI/CD, automated testing across framework and server versions, version compatibility checks, and release steps. Suggest improvements where you see repeated friction
 Help keep the integrations you work on healthy: monitor for upstream breaking changes, handle upgrades, triage incoming issues, and follow through after release
 Coordinate with adjacent teams, including DBX, when your work depends on driver, platform, or product capability, and escalate cross-team dependencies and risks early rather than working around them
 Collaborate with product management, product design, and other partners to understand what users need from an integration and how your work connects to the team's objectives
 Write clear documentation, give useful code reviews, share what you know with teammates, and follow through on your commitments
 Develop specialized knowledge of the Python or TypeScript AI builder ecosystems — frameworks, agent and retrieval patterns, vector search — and bring interesting developments back to the team
 Qualifications 
 3+ years of experience building backend systems, libraries, or other developer-facing software, with solid proficiency in Python and/or TypeScript
 Experience designing, writing, testing, and debugging software in a shared, long-lived code base, with an eye for the tests and documentation that make it maintainable
 Track record of delivering scoped projects reliably and on time, with growing independence and good judgment about when to ask for help
 Demonstrated ability to work on several projects at once and keep quality and commitments intact as priorities shift
 Clear interest in modern AI builder workflows and the developer tooling landscape: AI frameworks, agentic patterns, RAG and retrieval, embedding, or vector search
 Solid verbal and written technical communication, including the ability to write things down clearly for teammates and partners you won't always overlap with in real time
 Enjoys collaboration and being part of a close-knit team; is approachable, curious, and intellectually honest
 Eager to learn, with a strong technical foundation and an interest in deepening it
 Nice to Have 
 Open source contributions, especially any work that landed in a repository you don't own
 Experience building AI or framework integrations, MCP servers, agent skills, or plugins for agentic applications, professionally or as side projects
 Familiarity with the agentic AI tooling ecosystem (AI IDEs, CLIs, and assistants) and how developers integrate with it
 Experience with CI/CD and automated testing for libraries that support multiple versions or platforms
 Experience working with databases; familiarity with MongoDB query patterns
 Exposure to vector search, embedding pipelines, or index management
 Working knowledge of Java, Go, C#, or Rust
 Experience with container

title: Technical Account Manager
desc:
MongoDB Technical Account Managers are at the forefront of technical problem solving with key customers, working on some of the most complex and exciting application ecosystems built on the MongoDB platform. TAMs combine:
 Deep product knowledge and expertise across multiple domains 
 Polished technical communications
 Strong account leadership, with the ability to engage effectively at all levels of the customer
 Ability to not only proactively engage, but anticipate and preempt needs a customer may have or issues they could experience
 A high degree of ownership and willingness to go above and beyond for our customers
 The TAM’s primary remit is the cultivation of customer confidence and delivery of positive, account-wide technical outcomes that solve big customer problems while showcasing the capabilities of the MongoDB product portfolio. They do this through a systematic engagement process including deep discovery and the development of a roadmap of shared objectives. They are able to operate in complex environments where there may be shared or even ambiguous responsibilities between the customer and MongoDB. The TAM is able to shift gears between enabling, coaching and mentoring, and marshaling resources to get the right things done at the right time.
 The TAM also acts as the eyes and ears of the product team while working with marquee customers as they will sometimes surface new requirements or potential areas of opportunity for future development. They work closely with these teams to understand these requirements, manage expectations, and ensure MongoDB is staying one step ahead of customer needs.
 This role will be an early hire into the new Technical Account Management function and will help pioneer the new service offering for MongoDB.
 Successful candidates will have the flexibility to work around the schedules of customers with 100% uptime systems while enjoying the life/work balance MongoDB promotes.
 We are looking to speak to candidates who are based in Bengaluru for our hybrid working model.

desc:

Technical Service Engineers are experts in the entire MongoDB ecosystem - database server, drivers, cloud and infrastructure. desc:
About the Team
Would you like to be part of creating a unicorn within a unicorn? Solve some of the biggest challenges facing financial inclusion of Bharat? Well, then here’s your chance!
Financial Services (FS) is one of the biggest new bets we are taking at Meesho on the next 10x horizon opportunity for us. Just as Ant Financial did for Alibaba, and Mercado Pago did for Mercado Libre, our vision is to build financial services for Meesho, becoming our key growth and revenue driver.
We have found our Product-Market Fit and built and proved 0-1 and 1-10 journeys, Now looking for someone who can be the founding member of 10-100-1000 journey and this is possibly one of the most exciting and enriching experiences one could consider in their career.
As a Financial Services team, we always look at the bottom line. And the bottom line is - in this team, you should expect to have fun as you learn and grow.
About the Role
Lending is going to be our primary focus in this phase of our FS journey, and risk management is at the core of building any sustainable credit business at scale. Herein also lies potentially our biggest challenge for Meesho users: How do we assess risk of borrowers without any credit history? How can we leverage alternative information to better profile borrowers? How can we leverage our platform uniquely to create a sustained competitive advantage?
The Person will be responsible for driving the Policy, DS and analytics behind all these questions, from creating analytical frameworks, developing high quality analysis, driving insights and actions, and owning policy decisions.
In the early phases, your role will focus on refining initially implemented policy by Analyzing and Designing credit policies using Meesho platform data, bureau data, alternate data. Creating Scorecards and models for approval. 
Designing experiments to test cohort behavior and experimental policies.
Automate reporting and tracking of the portfolio on multiple levels , Ops performance measures, key performance indicators and associated drivers.

title: AM/M - Risk Analytics - User Lending
desc:
About the Team
Would you like to be part of creating a unicorn within a unicorn? Solve some of the biggest challenges facing financial inclusion of Bharat? Well, then here's your chance!
Financial Services (FS) is one of the biggest new bets we are taking at Meesho on the next 10x horizon opportunity for us. Just as Ant Financial did for Alibaba, and Mercado Pago did for Mercado Libre, our vision is to build financial services for Meesho, becoming our key growth and revenue driver.
We have found our Product-Market Fit, built and proved 0-1 and 1-10 journeys. Now looking for someone who can be the founding member of a 10-100-1000 journey, and this is possibly one of the most exciting and enriching experiences one could consider in their career.
About the Role
Meesho FS runs two lines of business: SME Lending, which offers Business Loans, and User Lending, which offers BNPL and Personal Loans (PL). 
User Lending is now our primary focus in this phase of our FS journey. We have 274Mn ATU, and risk management is at the core of building any sustainable credit business at scale - our being a captive audience means both Growth and Risk are an outcome of underwriting, which is owned by the Risk team.
Herein also lies one of our biggest challenges: how do we assess the risk of borrowers without any credit history or income data? How can we leverage alternative information to better profile borrowers? How can we leverage our platform uniquely to create a sustained competitive advantage?
This person will be responsible for driving the analytics behind these questions for User Lending - creating analytical frameworks, developing high quality analysis, driving insights and actions, and recommending policy decisions, across a well-established BNPL portfolio and a Personal Loans portfolio that is still scaling.
Your role will focus on:
Owning the risk for one or more segments of the portfolio while maintaining a healthy growth.
Analyzing credit policies using Meesho platform data, bureau data, SMS data, and other alternate data.
Creating policies, scorecards and models (Application Score, B-Score, Collection Scores) for BNPL and PL.
Designing experiments to test cohort behaviour, experimental policies, and new opportunities for growth.
Identifying pockets of risk within the portfolio that don't make sense, and identifying leading indicators / EWS.
Automating reporting and tracking of the portfolio at multiple levels - Ops performance measures, key performance indicators, and their drivers.
Refining credit policies based on data and creating new policies for unexplored segments, including building day-1 policies for Personal Loans as the product scales.
Configuring and testing rules in the real-time Business Rule Engine (BRE), and working with the Bureau Feature Store to define new underwriting features.

title: Data Scientist III (Team- Valmo)
desc:
About us
Meesho - Every story here begins with a spark of ambition and a touch of entrepreneurial magic. We're not just a platform — we're your partner in transforming dreams into reality.
Our Mission
Democratising internet commerce for everyone - Meesho started with a single idea in mind: to be an e-commerce destination for the next billion Indian consumers and enable small businesses to succeed online. We provide sellers with a range of industry-first benefits such as zero commission and affordable shipping costs, growing their business by tapping the company's massive customer base, state-of-the-art tech infrastructure, and pan-India logistics at cost through third-party logistics providers and our in-house logistics arm Valmo, in an 'Everyday Low Cost' channel for sellers.
Affordable, relatable merchandise mirroring local markets has helped us make inroads with first-time internet users in the country. We cater to an underserved and unique customer base and cover every serviceable pincode in the country. Our unique business model and continuous innovation have enabled us to become the first Indian horizontal e-commerce company.
Know more about Meesho here: https://www.meesho.io/
About Valmo and the Data Science Team
Valmo is Meesho's own logistics arm, built to give sellers and customers cutting-edge, low-cost logistics and supply chain support. Supply Chain Network Optimization sits at the heart of the Valmo Data Science team: we design and plan the network that moves Valmo's shipments every day, from first-mile pickup through sort centres and line haul to last-mile delivery. We use OR, MILP, stochastic optimisation, simulation, ML and DL across network design, first/middle/last-mile optimisation, capacity planning and delivery promise, and we build for the long term, not just today's problems. This role is for someone ready to execute at speed, with a growth mindset, to build and scale these models.
 About the Role
As a Data Scientist 3(Operations Research), you will own a workstream within Valmo network design — not just a model. You will be accountable for the North Star Metric of that workstream (cost per shipment, end-to-end shipment speed, network capacity utilisation, on-time delivery, delivery promise), set its OR/ML roadmap, and mentor DS1s and DS2s in delivering it. You will take ambiguous, loosely-defined business problems, decide which ones are worth solving, formulate them mathematically, and ship optimization systems that run Valmo's network every day. Workstreams span network design, routing and scheduling across the first, middle and last mile.

title: Engineering Manager -Backend
desc:
About Meesho 
Mission and Vision 
Meesho is India’s fastest-growing internet commerce company, driven by the mission to democratize internet commerce for everyone (DICE). Our vision is to enable 100 million small businesses and entrepreneurs in India to succeed online, making online commerce accessible to all. This core purpose guides us in empowering sellers across the country and bringing a diverse range of products to first-time internet shoppers. By leveraging technology and a unique zero commission model, Meesho has opened the doors of e-commerce to millions who were previously underserved. 
Technological Scale & Innovation
 At Meesho, technology is at the heart of our success. We have invested in a scalable infrastructure and innovative solutions to meet the demands of a vast user base and complex marketplace. Some key highlights include: 
Massive Scale: Our backend systems handle millions of orders per day from across India, reaching about 5% of all Indian households, all with near-zero downtime to date. Achieving this level of reliability and performance in a hyper-growth environment is a testament to our engineering excellence. 
 Marketplace Reach: Over 1.75 million sellers are registered on Meesho’s platform, supported by our state-of-the-art tech infrastructure and pan-India logistics network. This wide reach — covering virtually every serviceable pin code in the country — presents unique engineering challenges in areas like search, personalization, and payments at scale.
 Scalable Architecture: We continually innovate our architecture for growth.. Our quest to serve a billion Indian users has helped us evolve our technologies from a monolith to microservices to now a high scale federated architecture. This evolution allows us to build and deploy features rapidly while maintaining stability for a fast-growing user base. 
Cutting-edge Tech Stack: Our platform is built using modern, open-source technologies on the cloud while ensuring high efficiency. We strategically choose proven tools (for example, Java and Golang for services, Kafka for messaging, Dragonfly and Redis for caching, ScyllaDB, MySQL and Mongo for Data) and leverage GCP infrastructure to ensure high performance, reliability, and flexibility. By focusing on the right tools for the right problems, we innovate pragmatically rather than chasing every new tech hype, which helps us solve real-world problems effectively. 
Engineering Culture & Challenges 
Engineering at Meesho is driven by a bold and inclusive culture that values innovation, ownership, and continuous improvement. We believe that building great products goes hand-in-hand with building a great team. Key aspects of our engineering culture include: 
Long Term Thinking: We believe in thinking for tomorrow while building for today, this approach has helped us not only to handle and evolve for scale but also focus on extensibility and stability by investing in the platform
Lightspeed: We prioritize rapid iteration and delivery. Engineers are encouraged to ship fast and refine continuously, as we value in order to learn and adapt quickly. 
Continuous Improvement: We view failures and bugs as opportunities to improve. A blameless post-mortem culture ensures that mistakes become lessons, fostering an environment where learning from failure drives resilience and innovation.
 Ownership Mindset: Every engineer is empowered to act like an owner. We instill a “Founder’s Mindset,” encouraging engineers to take end-to-end ownership of projects and drive them with an entrepreneurial spirit. This means our teams proactively identify problems and champion solutions, just as a founder would for their own product. 
Engineering at Meesho is more than just writing code – it's about solving complex, impactful problems at an unprecedented scale. Our engineers tackle challenging use cases (from enabling real-time logistics across India to optimizing a vast product catalog for the next billion users), making a tangible impact on millions of entrepreneurs and customers. We maintain a
professional, yet passionate work environment where the drive to innovate is balanced with a pragmatic approach to problem-solving. 
About the Role
We are looking for Engineering Manager well-versed with emerging technologies to join our team.
 As an Engineering Manager, you will ensure consistency and quality by shaping the right strategies. You will keep an eye on all engineering projects and ensure all duties are fulfilled . You will analyse other employees’ tasks and carry on collaborations effectively. You will also transform newbies into experts and build reports on the progress of all projects.

title: Manager – GTM & Sales Strategy, Meesho AI Services (MAS)
desc:
About the Team
MAS's mission is to accelerate the build and deployment of an AI workforce for every business — from kirana to conglomerate. Our vision is to deliver a billion-plus workflows through our agents in ways that drive real client outcomes, not automation for its own sake.
We go deep rather than wide. Today that means known, process-defined, repeatable service workflows — inbound contact-centre work (calls, chats, tickets), plus the outbound work that behaves like a cost workflow rather than a conversion one (lead qualification and verification, not lead conversion) — anywhere we can benchmark against a cost line the client already feels, guarantee savings, and hold the quality bar. We're deliberately building a technology company, not an AI BPO: models are a commodity, so our moat is the workflow knowledge, integrations, and client relationships that only come from actually running the work — not a generic AI layer bolted onto a call centre.
We've proven this model works — with marquee clients across consumer durables, auto, and D2C/marketplace businesses — and we're still early. We'll keep evolving it as we go, staying client-first rather than assuming we already have the answer. This is a 0–1 business inside Meesho: no fixed playbook, high ownership, and the ground floor of how India's enterprises adopt AI-led operations.
About the Role
This role is for a GTM generalist who thrives in ambiguity, is genuinely excited about AI-led offerings, and wants to build the full range of enterprise sales skills — with an eye on growing into a closer and sales leader over time, or moving into Business/GTM Operations. Both are real paths from this seat.
You own the middle mile of the deal: the stretch between a qualified conversation and a close-ready opportunity. That means deep client discovery, mapping who really decides, understanding how a client's teams actually work today, and making sure the deal never goes cold on your watch — following up, keeping momentum, and setting up the closer to walk into the room fully briefed. Our central team owns top-of-funnel lead-gen, but this isn't a purely inbound or coordination role — you'll still make cold calls and run early client meetings yourself when a deal needs it.
A lot of enterprise AI-services deals across this market stall before signature for a simple reason: nobody on the deal ever gets deep enough into the account to know what the client is actually buying, or who really decides. That's exactly the gap this role exists to close — the middle mile is where deals live or die.

• At least 2 years in strategic or complex enterprise GTM, account management, or programme delivery — where you owned client relationships, not just supported them

managed to do it

relationship

need to move on them

• Experience at a top-tier consulting firm; owning complex analytical problem-solving, structuring ambiguous mandates, and being accountable for outcomes is strongly valued.
Who You Are

• You are direct; you say what you actually think, including to people more senior than you
• You are comfortable with ambiguity and genuinely energised by environments where the answer isn't obvious
• You move with urgency and bring others with you through influence, not authority
Why Sarvam?
Sarvam is a fast-moving, high talent-density team building full-stack AI for India, working on problems that push the frontiers of AI with real population-scale impact.
• Work alongside researchers, engineers, builders, and business leaders who move fast and hold each other to a very high bar

title: Data Scientist - Evaluations, Chanakya
desc:
About Sarvam
Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India's full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV, and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India's leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC, and LIC.
About the Role
This is an intellectually demanding role. The Data Scientist anchors the evaluations function for this vertical — designing, building, and maintaining evaluation frameworks that measure model and system quality in operational context. You are not running standard benchmarks. You are building domain-specific eval harnesses for high-stakes use cases where a wrong answer carries real consequences.
You will work closely with the MLOps Engineer, the PM, and the deployment team. The evaluations you design are the mechanism by which the team determines whether what we've built is good enough to deploy — and whether it stays good after deployment.
What You'll Do
• Design and build evaluation frameworks for Sarvam's AI outputs across domain-specific requirements: document comprehension, command summarisation, geospatial reasoning, enterprise workflow automation, and others as they emerge
• Define quality metrics in collaboration with domain experts and clients; translate operational requirements into measurable, defensible signals
• Run structured evaluation cycles pre- and post-deployment; build dashboards that surface model quality in production
• Identify failure modes, edge cases, and distribution shifts — with the bias of someone looking for what's wrong, not confirming what's right
• Collaborate with the MLOps Engineer to operationalise eval pipelines — automated, triggered by deployment events, versioned, and reproducible
• Build and manage domain-specific datasets for fine-tuning, evaluation, and benchmarking — including human annotation workflows where needed
• Publish internal findings and quality reports that feed the product and engineering roadmap
What We're Looking For
• 3–6 years in data science, ML research, or applied AI; at least 2 years working with LLMs in production contexts
• Strong statistics and probability fundamentals — you understand what makes an evaluation valid and what makes it misleading
• Experience designing evaluation frameworks from scratch: custom metrics, inter-rater reliability, red-teaming methodologies

title: Infrastructure SRE - HPC
desc:
About Sarvam
Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India’s full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV, and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India’s leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC, and LIC.
About the Role
Sarvam runs a large, multi-vendor GPU fleet that serves two demanding workloads on the same physical infrastructure: training jobs that span hundreds of GPUs and must run uninterrupted for weeks, and inference services that must hold a flat p99 under production load. Keeping both healthy at once is a hard, specialized reliability problem, and it is the problem this team exists to solve.
This is not a Kubernetes administration role. We assume Kubernetes fluency as a baseline. The difficulty lies above and below it - in parallel filesystems under heavy checkpoint load, in RDMA fabrics that degrade quietly, in NCCL hangs whose root cause may be the network or the kernel, in driver and firmware drift across heterogeneous hardware, and in distributed training failures that masquerade as infrastructure faults.
We are hiring a team of specialists rather than a set of identical generalists. This posting covers five areas of focus. We expect candidates to bring genuine depth in one and working fluency across the others, because on a shared fleet a storage problem often first appears as a training hang, and the engineer on call must route an incident correctly before anyone can resolve it.
When you apply, please indicate the area of focus that best matches your experience. Strong generalists are welcome; we will place you where your depth is most useful.
What You’ll Do
 - Operate the GPU fleet end to end across training and serving - provisioning, observability, capacity, and fleet health.
 - Hold a meaningful on-call rotation, write runbooks that hold up under pressure, and drive postmortems that produce durable fixes.
 - Build the internal tooling the team relies on, rather than operating off-the-shelf systems alone.
 - Partner with ML and platform teams to keep large runs alive and serving latency predictable.
What We're Looking For
 - 5+ years in infrastructure or site reliability engineering, including 2+ years operating GPU clusters at scale.*
 - Demonstrated on-call ownership of infrastructure that mattered, with a track record of postmortems that led to real change.
 - Proficiency in Python or Go, used to build and maintain internal tooling.
 - Working fluency across all five areas of focus below - enough to recognize, triage, and route a problem outside your specialty, even if the fix belongs to a teammate.
* For the Storage and Fabric areas of focus, we will weigh deep domain expertise against the GPU-cluster requirement; exceptional specialists with less direct GPU-fleet time are encouraged to apply.
Bring depth in one of the five areas below; expect to be conversational across the rest.
 1. Distributed high-performance storage — operate a parallel filesystem (Lustre, GPFS, WEKA, or BeeGFS) at scale and keep it from stalling under checkpoint-write storms.
 2. Fabric & RDMA networking — InfiniBand or RoCE health, NVLink/NVSwitch topology, and RDMA debugging that catches degradation before the workload feels it.
 3. GPU systems reliability — NCCL debugging, driver and firmware lifecycle across a mixed fleet, and DCGM-based node health at scale.
 4. Kubernetes platform reliability — the GPU operator stack, scheduling (Slurm-on-k8s or pure k8s), multi-tenant isolation, and cost/SLO primitives.
 5. Training & inference workload reliability — hang and straggler detection, checkpoint/restart, and protecting serving p99 with HA and DR.
Bonus Points

Sarvam runs a large, multi-vendor GPU fleet that serves two demanding workloads on the same physical infrastructure: training jobs that span hundreds of GPUs, and inference services that must hold a flat p99 under production load. This role builds the platform that sits on top of that fleet - the scheduling, scaling, multi-tenancy, serving, and self-service layers that let our ML teams use thousands of GPUs without a human in the loop for every job.
This is the build side of infrastructure, not the operate side. Our SREs keep the fleet reliable and carry the pager; you build the systems that make the fleet usable - and that make it break less in the first place. The work is heavy software engineering: you will design and ship control-plane services, scheduler integrations, autoscaling controllers, the inference-serving platform, RBAC and quota systems, observability and cost tooling, and the CLI and APIs ML engineers touch every day. You will treat the platform as a product and its internal users as customers.
You should be a strong systems engineer who is fluent in Kubernetes at the controller and internals level, comfortable in Go or Python, and literate in the GPU-specific constraints - MIG and GPU sharing, gang scheduling, topology-aware placement, RDMA - that make this different from a generic cloud platform.
What You’ll Do
This is the surface area of the platform. You won't own all of it at once - you'll take a capability and build it end to end - but you should be excited by most of it.

 - Multi-tenancy, RBAC, and isolation. The tenant model and namespacing, RBAC and policy, quota and fair-share enforcement, MIG / MPS / time-slicing exposed as self-service tiers, secrets and credential management, and audit logging.
 - Networking components. Platform-level network plumbing - CNI configuration and custom components, ingress and service routing, RDMA / SR-IOV exposure into pods, tenant network policy and segmentation, and multi-cluster connectivity.
 - Observability and cost tooling. The metrics, logging, and tracing pipeline as a platform feature with cardinality managed at fleet scale.
 - The storage and data path. Abstractions over the parallel filesystem, caching tiers, volume provisioning, and data-locality-aware placement.
 - Developer experience and self-service. The layer ML engineers actually touch - CLI, SDK, and APIs, job-submission abstractions and inner-loop tooling.

title: Performance Engineer, Kernels
desc:
PERFORMANCE ENGINEER, KERNELS
Part of Sarvam's Performance Engineering team. We are hiring two specialized performance roles - Kernels (this posting) and Inference (companion posting). They are a vertical stack: the kernels team authors the µs-level GPU code, and the inference team integrates it into a running serving stack and owns the system-level numbers. If your depth genuinely spans both, apply to either and tell us - but most candidates are strongest in one, and we hire for that depth.
Location: [Bengaluru / Chennai / Hybrid / On-site] · Team: Performance Engineering · Level: Senior
ABOUT THE TEAM
Sarvam serves multiple model families - small and large LLMs, Mixture-of-Experts, streaming Indic ASR, and multimodal - across a multi-node, multi-tenant fleet on H100 / H200 / B200. The Performance Engineering team owns the numbers the rest of the company plans against: how fast we serve, how much it costs, and how much we get out of every GPU. This team works at the intersection of the serving runtime, the kernel layer, and the SRE org that keeps the fleet alive.
ABOUT THE ROLE
You will own the kernel layer. Where stock libraries - cuBLAS, cuDNN, FlashAttention, out-of-the-box Triton - leave performance on the table, you will author the custom CUDA, DSL-based, and PTX kernels that close the gap.
This is a hard, narrow, high-leverage role. We hire engineers who have shipped kernels that beat published baselines on real workloads, not engineers who have used kernels. When your code lands, production p99 moves, and you own the explanation of why.
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
 - 5+ years in ML systems, with 2+ years authoring production CUDA kernels. You have a kernel in production that beat the prior baseline by a measurable margin.
 - CUDA at kernel-authoring level: thread-block sizing, shared-memory layout, warp primitives, async copies (cp.async, TMA), and MMA selection.
 - CUTLASS / CuTe DSL at a modify-and-extend level, with comfort in the layout algebra.
 - PTX at a debug-and-modify level - you have inserted hand-written PTX where the compiler missed.
 - Nsight Compute and Systems fluency: you read a roofline plot and propose the fix.
 - Attention kernels: you have authored or modified at least one (FlashAttention-family, paged, MLA, sliding-window, or sparse).
 - Multi-architecture awareness: what changes from Hopper to Blackwell (TMA, WGMMA, tcgen05).
STRONG PLUSES
 - Communication kernels - NCCL / NVSHMEM authoring, custom collectives, expert-parallel dispatch (DeepEP-style), AFD bipartite comms (StepMesh-style), KV transfer (DualPath / Mooncake). Strongly desired; dedicated comms-specialist headcount is expected later.
 - Open-source kernel contributions - FlashAttention, CUTLASS examples, vLLM / SGLang kernels, DeepEP, Mooncake, or non-trivial Triton work. For this role, the GitHub filter is the highest-yield signal.
 - tcgen05, TMA, CTA-cluster launch and distributed shared memory, async pipelining, and the FP4/microscaling paths
 - Grace-side host-path optimization on GH200 / GB200.

You will produce, and defend, the latency and throughput numbers the company plans against, and you will spend significant time in cross-team work with architecture co-design, the kernels team, the model team, and SRE.
Your scoreboard: TTFT (p50 / p95 / p99), TPOT, throughput, GPU utilization, and cost per million tokens.
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

STRONG PLUSES

title: DevOps Engineer
desc:

You should be a hands-on DevOps engineer fluent in Kubernetes, comfortable with cloud infrastructure (AWS primarily, Azure secondarily), and literate in the networking and CI/CD concerns that keep a multi-cluster, multi-tenant environment running. You will work closely with the engineers building the harness; your job is to make their work shippable, observable, and operable at scale.

• Networking and connectivity. Manage platform-level network plumbing — CNI configuration, ingress and service routing, network policies, and secure cross-cluster and on-prem connectivity via VPN tunnels, peering, and transit paths.

• Provisioning and infrastructure-as-code. Keep environments standing reproducibly — Terraform / Crossplane, image management, and multi-vendor cluster bring-up alongside the team.
What We’re Looking For
• 3+ years in DevOps, SRE, or platform / infrastructure engineering, with hands-on ownership of systems you ran and improved - not just scripts that worked once.

Bonus Points

title: Deployment Strategist
desc:

Closing that gap is the hardest problem in enterprise AI, and it is what Deployment Strategists at Sarvam do. You own the arc of a customer engagement, from the first proof of concept through to their systems running live, handling millions of real conversations across Indian languages and delivering the outcomes we signed up to. If Sarvam's technology is going to reach a billion people rather than sit in a slide deck, it happens through this team.
Every large institution is its own environment, with its own core systems, telephony, CRM, compliance perimeter and operational reality. You work out what it takes for an AI system to hold up inside that specific environment, run the programme, and stay accountable until it is live and performing.
Our engagements run from focused proofs of concept to multi-year programmes inside India's biggest enterprises and government departments, worth crores and reaching millions of people. We are hiring across levels to cover that range.
ABOUT SARVAM
Sarvam is India's leading full-stack AI company, building sovereign AI infrastructure and applications purpose-built for India. Headquartered in Bengaluru and founded by leading AI researchers, Sarvam builds foundational models for Indian languages, enterprise AI platforms, and voice-first AI agents that serve hundreds of millions of Indians. Sarvam is backed by top-tier investors and works with national and state governments, large enterprises, and developers across the country. We are building the AI layer for a billion people.
WHAT THIS ROLE PROMISES YOU
You own the outcome
You are not tracking someone else's plan. You own the scope, the timeline, and whether the numbers land. When a deployment works, it is because you made it work.
The room where AI meets the Indian economy

title: Agent Engineer
desc:
The distance between an AI system that works and one that millions of people rely on every day is where the real engineering lives. Crossing it is what Agent Engineers at Sarvam do.
The agents you build go into live operation at India's largest banks, insurers, NBFCs and government departments, and at some of the country's fastest-growing companies, handling millions of real interactions, measured against outcomes the customer wants to drive.
The hard part is not the first version. It is everything after: mapping the full space of what an agent has to handle so the scenarios that matter are covered by design rather than discovered in production, engineering for the failure modes instead of the happy path, and building the evals and instrumentation that make quality measurable, so drift surfaces in the data rather than in a customer escalation.
We treat agents as code. Not prompts someone tweaks in a console, but engineered artifacts: versioned, reviewed, and held to a regression suite, where you can reason about what a change will do and roll it back if you are wrong. Anyone who has watched an AI system quietly decay because nobody could tell which change broke it understands why this matters.
And then doing it again for the next customer, faster, because you built the first one to be repeatable.
ABOUT SARVAM
Sarvam is India's leading full-stack AI company, building sovereign AI infrastructure and applications purpose-built for India. Headquartered in Bengaluru and founded by leading AI researchers, Sarvam builds foundational models for Indian languages, enterprise AI platforms, and voice-first AI agents that serve hundreds of millions of Indians. Sarvam is backed by top-tier investors and works with national and state governments, large enterprises, and developers across the country. We are building the AI layer for a billion people.
WHAT THIS ROLE PROMISES YOU
Production, at real scale
Not prototypes, not demos. Systems in live operation at some of India's largest institutions, carrying real volume, measured against outcomes the customer has signed up to. You will see the consequences of your engineering decisions within days.
You work at the source
Sarvam builds the whole stack: the foundational models, the infrastructure they run on, and the products on top of them. When a deployment needs something that does not exist yet, whether that is model behaviour, an infrastructure capability or a product change, you are not filing a ticket with a vendor and waiting on a roadmap. You are in a room with the people who built it. Anyone who has delivered AI on top of someone else's black box knows how much difference that makes.
A genuinely broad surface
Sarvam's products span conversational AI, agentic workflows, intelligent document processing, and content, including dubbing and document translation. You will own a motion and go deep in it, and the depth you build travels well as products mature and new ones ship.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
 - Build production agents on the Sarvam stack: prompts, system design, workflows, tool integrations, and evals.
 - Map the space the agent has to cover. Work out the scenarios that matter, how each should be handled, and where the edges are, so coverage is designed rather than discovered later.
 - Build the proof of concept when a customer wants to see it work before committing at scale, and get to a convincing result fast.
 - Integrate into systems that were never designed for this: core banking, CRM, ticketing, telephony, and whatever else the customer runs.
 - Own quality end to end. Define what good means for the use case, build the evals that measure it, and close the gap until the numbers hold.
 - Engineer agents like software. Version them, review them, and hold them to a regression suite, so quality does not depend on who last edited a prompt.
 - Tune for the constraints that decide whether a system survives production: accuracy, cost, reliability, and performance under real load.
 - Design for scale and consistency from the outset. Systems that behave the same on the hundred-thousandth interaction as the first, and that are instrumented well enough for anyone to see when they are not.
 - Take a proven pattern into a new customer and make it fit their environment, at pace and at quality.
 - At senior levels, own the technical build playbooks and the technical quality bar for a motion, and bring partner engineers up to it.
WHO YOU ARE

title: GTM Strategy - Chanakya
desc:
About team: 
Chanakya is Sarvam AI's specialised, self-contained vertical for national security and institutions of national importance. It carries its own pricing, business, product, engineering, custom-model and vendor functions under one roof — a complete unit built to solve the most complex problems in the strategic sector: the three armed forces, intelligence agencies, financial regulators, and institutions of national importance such as central ministries and national policy bodies.
What we deploy here must be at strategic parity or higher — anything less is a national-security risk. That standard is the reason Chanakya is a small, exceptionally high-performing team inside Sarvam, and the reason we are deliberate about who joins it.
Why this is one of the most consequential seats in Indian AI
01 — NATIONAL IMPACT
You sit where it all gets decided.
These systems are deployed inside the institutions that safeguard the country. The potential for national impact is not abstract — it is at the core of how the strategic sector reasons, decides, and acts. Few roles anywhere in Indian technology carry this weight.
02 — UNPARALLELED LEARNING
Full-stack, end to end — nowhere else does this exist.
Every deployment runs the entire stack: understanding a customer's real requirement, architecting and customising the stack for it, and where needed building and fine-tuning models, shaping training data, and inventing data representations for extraordinarily complex data, workflows and applications. You touch nearly the whole arc of the work. This experience sets you apart — whether you go on to found a company, or become a business or technology leader in the years ahead, at Sarvam or beyond.
03 — A PATH TO LEADERSHIP
These are leadership seats in the making.
Chanakya's functions are being built out now. We are looking for people who will grow into the leaders of these emerging functions — every one of these roles is a route to leading a part of the vertical, not just filling it.
Where we are. This is not a leap into the unknown. Chanakya has already achieved product–market fit to a meaningful degree, has significant revenue booked, and has large strategic projects officially underway. Things are structured and going well.
The opportunity. This is a genuine zero-to-one journey — but one taken within the reach, talent and standing of a company like Sarvam. You get the ambition and ownership of building something new, backed by the full weight of Sarvam's capability and presence. The golden opportunity: to help build out and lead the emerging functions of Chanakya, with a clear growth path ahead. 
Where client-facing instinct meets technical depth — working directly with the founders.
You will bring your client-facing judgement and technical fluency together to shape and drive Chanakya's go-to-market, working closely with the leadership and the founders to get it built.
•Strong technical foundation plus sharp commercial and strategic instincts.
•Comfortable in the room with senior institutional stakeholders and with our own engineers.
•Entrepreneurial temperament — owns outcomes end to end.
The bar. 
Across every one of these roles, we are looking for people who want to change the world and build something of national consequence — and who will grow into the leaders of Chanakya's verticals. If that is you, the ceiling here is set only by your ambition.
Base: Delhi NCR, with travel across India. All roles involve working inside restricted environments and travelling to client sites at short notice.

title: Motion Designer
desc:
ABOUT SARVAM
Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India’s full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV, and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India’s leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC, and LIC.
ABOUT THE ROLE
Sarvam’s brand is already an argument about motion — it just hasn’t been allowed to move yet.
The monogram is a gateway that emerges — layered circles resolving out of mandala geometry into a single threshold form. The palette isn’t a set of swatches; it’s a continuous run from blue to orange, built to suggest progression and responsive state. Both of those ideas are about change over time. Both are currently being made mostly in stills.
We want the person who resolves that. Not someone to animate a logo once for a launch, but someone who decides how this brand behaves — how it enters, how it responds, how a gradient moves without becoming wallpaper — and then builds that language across films, web and product.
It’s a rare brief: a real identity with real motion logic baked into it, and nobody has run at it yet.
WHAT YOU’LL DO
 - Define the motion language, not just the motion. Timing, easing, entrances, transitions, how the monogram behaves and how the gradient travels — documented and reusable, so the next fifty assets don’t start from zero.
 - Make the films. Model launches, product announcements, research drops, event opens, brand pieces. Concept, board, animate, edit, sound, deliver — you’ll own the shot end to end.
 - Make the product move too. Web animation, scroll behaviour, UI micro-interactions, demo and walkthrough videos. This is the half of the role that keeps the other half honest: motion that ships inside a live surface has constraints a film doesn’t.
 - Hand off cleanly to engineering. Lottie, Rive, sprite sequences, or a spec an engineer can actually build from. Work that dies in After Effects doesn’t count.
 - Solve the hard one: visualising speech. Our products are conversational — voice agents across 11 Indian languages, code-switching mid-sentence. Showing listening, thinking, speaking and switching, without falling back on a generic waveform, is the most interesting motion problem in the building.
 - Use AI properly in the pipeline. Generative video, boards and previz, roto, upscaling, variation. You should already be doing this, with a clear sense of where it saves a week and where it costs you the shot.
 - Work across the whole company. Design, marketing, product, research, founders. Rough briefs, hard launch dates, and work that still holds up at the end of it.
WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR
 - 3+ years in motion design, in-house or at a studio, with a reel that shows both narrative work and work that shipped inside a product or website.
 - Deep After Effects. Shape layers, expressions, proper rigging — not template-and-swap. Plus real editing chops in Premiere or Resolve.
 - Figma is non-negotiable. Motion here starts inside the design system, not beside it.
 - Illustrator and Photoshop at working depth — you’ll be building and cleaning your own assets.
 - Fundamentals over flourish. Timing, weight, staging, anticipation, and how type behaves in motion. We will notice your easing curves.
 - Native fluency with AI tools in a professional motion workflow, and a point of view about it.
 - System thinking. Evidence you’ve taken a static identity and extended it into motion — or taken a motion system somewhere its guidelines hadn’t gone.
 - A real stake in this. You should care specifically about what Indian design deserves to look like in motion — and be a little impatient that it mostly doesn’t look like that yet.
BONUS POINTS
 - 3D — Blender or Cinema 4D, especially for abstract systems, geometry and product visualisation
 - Real-time or code-based motion: Rive, three.js, GLSL, TouchDesigner, Houdini
 - Sound design and mix — or at least strong instincts about audio driving picture
 - Indic typography in motion: animating Devanagari, Tamil or Kannada without breaking the letterforms
HOW TO APPLY
Send a reel — 90 seconds is plenty — plus a breakdown of what you did on each piece. Three shots you own completely beat a beautifully cut reel of team work. If one of them had to survive a real constraint — an engineer, a file size, a deadline, a language you don’t read — lead with that.

title: Software Engineer - Model API Platform
desc:
About Sarvam
Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India's full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India's leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC and LIC.
About the role
Sarvam's model APIs (ASR, TTS, Vision, LLM, Translate) are how developers and enterprises ship products on our foundation models. The platform handles tens of millions of API calls every day, over HTTP and WebSockets, with metering, billing, prepaid wallets and rate-limiting all part of the same stack.
We are hiring a Software Engineer to own major parts of this platform end to end, working closely with the Staff Engineer who leads its architecture. You will take an area such as speech to text pipeline,or text to speech pipeline, and be accountable for its reliability, performance and end-to-end latencies. This role is for someone who is obsessed with latencies, optimizes services and network paths to shave off milliseconds, ships fast, reasons from first principles, and treats AI as the default way to get engineering work done.
What you will do
Own a platform area end to end
• Own one or more major parts of the platform, such as the WebSocket streaming layer, a speech recognition pipeline, or text to speech pipeline: build, operate and improve them.
• Turn loosely defined goals into RFCs, milestones and shipped results, and write down the decisions and trade-offs.
• Be accountable after launch: on-call, incident response, root-cause analysis and follow-through on fixes.
• Make the call when a decision is needed, and own the outcome.
• Obsessed with latencies, dissecting existing services to understand the system, and tuning the right knobs to optimize performance.
• Bring services across without regressions in customer-facing APIs, latency or reliability.
Build real-time and model-serving pipelines
• Build and operate streaming infrastructure: WebSocket connections, long-lived sessions queue-based batch processing, backpressure and low-latency model invocation.
• Engineer audio pipelines: TTS chunking around model context limits, sample-rate conversion and format encoding, and VAD-based silence detection for ASR.
• Hold your services to sub-100ms latency SLOs in a multi-tenant environment, and know where every millisecond goes.
Think in systems and from first principles
• Reasons from constraints: latency budgets per hop, throughput, cost per request, failure modes and tenant isolation.
• Use back-of-the-envelope estimates to decide what to build, what to optimize and what to leave alone.
• Prefer simple designs you can fully explain over clever ones you cannot.
• Build in observability from day one: logging, metrics and tracing that let anyone debug production quickly.
Raise the bar for the team
• Strengthen the integration testing harness so the team can ship fast without breaking customer-facing APIs.
• Partner with the Inference and MLOps teams on making model serving fast, reliable and operable.
• Mentor junior engineers through RFC reviews, code review and pairing.
• Practice design-first, documentation-first engineering: RFCs before code, no tribal knowledge.
What we are looking for
• 4–6 years of building and operating production backend systems.
• At least one service you owned end to end under real load, including what broke and what you changed.
• Strong distributed-systems fundamentals: concurrency, networking, queues, caching, consistency and failure modes.
• Experience with low-latency or high-throughput services, and comfort reasoning about p95 and p99 latency.
• Solid fundamentals with a relational database and a cache, such as PostgreSQL and Redis: schema design, query performance and caching strategy.
• Fluency in at least one backend language and willingness to work in both Python and Golang.
• Experience running services with containers, CI/CD and production monitoring.
• Daily, hands-on use of AI tools in your engineering workflow, with concrete examples of what you automated or sped up.
• A bias for action: fast on reversible decisions, careful on irreversible ones.
• Clear writing, especially RFCs and design docs that others can act on.
Good to have (not required)
• Voice AI or real-time audio experience: WebSockets, WebRTC, streaming ASR or TTS, or audio processing with FFmpeg or pyav, codecs, sample rates and VAD.
• Production experience in Go, or in Python with FastAPI.
• Experience serving LLM, ASR, TTS or vision models in production.
• Experience building metering, billing, wallet or payments infrastructure.
• Running services on Kubernetes in production.
• Time at an early- or growth-stage startup.
Why Sarvam
• A fast-moving, high talent-density team building full-stack AI for India, with real population-scale impact.
• Researchers, engineers, builders and business leaders who move fast and hold each other to a very high bar.
• High ownership and high impact from day one.

title: Software Development Engineer - Tejas
desc:
Enterprises want agents that can do real work on their own data. That data sits across documents, databases and business systems that were never built for agents to read, and today's agents forget most of what they learn once a session ends.
Our team builds Sarvam's context engine to solve both problems. The knowledge side brings an enterprise's data together so agents can search it, navigate it and cite where an answer came from. The memory side lets agents remember what they learn over time, about individual users, about teams, and across the organisation. We want both to keep improving as they are used.
Knowledge and memory for agents is a rapidly evolving field. We want to build at the frontier of it, and to show with measurable results that our approach does better than traditional ones.
ABOUT SARVAM
Sarvam is India's leading full-stack AI company, building sovereign AI infrastructure and applications purpose-built for India. Headquartered in Bengaluru and founded by leading AI researchers, Sarvam builds foundational models for Indian languages, enterprise AI platforms, and voice-first AI agents that serve hundreds of millions of Indians. Sarvam is backed by top-tier investors and works with national and state governments, large enterprises, and developers across the country. We are building the AI layer for a billion people.
WHAT THIS ROLE PROMISES YOU
You will join a small team and own large parts of the platform. The work is driven by real customer deployments, so what you build gets used quickly and you see what works and what does not. You will also work closely with the teams building Sarvam's models, document AI and inference, which makes it much easier to solve problems that cut across the stack.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
 - Build and run the ingestion pipeline that parses, extracts and indexes large volumes of documents, and keep it reliable when files are messy and external services fail.
 - Connect to databases and enterprise systems so agents can work with structured records as well as documents.
 - Design how enterprise data is modelled, including the ontology, matching the same entity across sources, and tracing every value back to where it came from.
 - Build the retrieval tools agents call, with search, filters and citations, and make them fast and cheap enough for agents to use heavily.
 - Build memory for agents at the level of a user, a team and the whole organisation: how it is written, stored, retrieved and kept accurate over time.
 - Run evals, find where answers go wrong, and keep iterating until quality improves.
 - Work with product and forward-deployed engineers to turn what one customer needs into something the platform does for every customer.
 - Write design docs and keep decisions documented.
Our production stack is Go, with Temporal, OpenSearch and Postgres.
WHO YOU ARE
We are hiring at 3 to 5 years of experience.
 - You have built and run backend or data systems in production, and you have fixed them when they broke.
 - You are strong in at least one backend language. Our core is in Go, so Go experience is a plus, and you should be happy to work in it every day.
 - You have good fundamentals in data modelling and PostgreSQL.
 - You have worked on long-running pipelines and know how to make them safe to retry and recover.
 - You have worked on search or retrieval and know how to debug why the right result did not come back.
 - You use AI coding tools every day and have a good sense of where they help and where they don't.
 - You care about measuring quality, and you are comfortable building the evals to do it.
BONUS POINTS
 - Experience with knowledge graphs, ontologies, entity resolution or structured extraction.
 - Experience building memory for agents or LLM applications.
 - Document processing, such as OCR, layout or table extraction.
 - Connectors or change data capture for ERP, CRM or other enterprise systems.
 - Building on MCP, or serving LLMs and embedding models in production.
 - On-prem or air-gapped deployments.
 - Experience at an early- or growth-stage startup.

title: Infrastructure Engineer

About the role
You keep the infrastructure behind Sarvam’s products running. You handle day-to-day operations — deployments, provisioning, access, incidents and cost questions — and you are expected to automate that work away.
We hire for one instinct above everything else: you notice something done by hand every day, ask why it can’t run itself, and build the thing that removes it — a script, a pipeline step, a bot, a small Kubernetes operator, or an AI agent that does the work. Operations is a large part of this role, and it is where you find what is worth automating.
As you automate your own toil away, more of your time goes into platform and automation work.
Products you may work on
Sarvam builds across a broad range of AI products: voice agents, coding agents, coworker agents, dubbing, our API platform, and the real-time voice and WebRTC infrastructure underneath them, among many others. You will work on the infrastructure behind them.
Responsibilities
• Own infrastructure operations across Sarvam’s products: deployments, provisioning requests, access, environment issues, cost questions
• Respond to incidents, write the runbook or postmortem afterwards, and fix the cause
• Automate repeated work: turn manual steps into pipeline jobs, Terraform modules, templates or self-service for product teams
• Build AI-assisted automations: agents that triage alerts, summarise incidents, review routine changes or answer product teams’ infrastructure questions, with a human approving anything risky

As an AI company, we are building AI agents into our own operations, to plan and review infrastructure changes, triage alerts and handle routine issues, with engineers setting the guardrails.
About the role
You are an infrastructure engineer whose first instinct is security, and who builds rather than only operates. You have worked on banking, fintech, payments or similarly regulated products, where a misconfiguration is an incident and an audit is routine. Here you set what “secure” means across Sarvam’s infrastructure and build the automation that enforces it, so security is a property of the pipeline rather than a review step. You work closely with the compliance team.
This is a hands-on role: most of your time goes into building, and you guide engineering teams across Sarvam on security — setting standards, reviewing security-relevant work and mentoring engineers.
Responsibilities
• Define and enforce security baselines for Kubernetes, cloud accounts, container images and CI/CD across all clouds
• Write the policy gates in the delivery pipeline (OPA / Conftest, Kyverno or equivalent): network exposure, IAM, image provenance, secrets, data residency
• Own secrets and workload identity: Vault or cloud-native equivalents, rotation, short-lived and scoped credentials, no long-lived keys
• Build detection and response: runtime security (Falco / Tetragon or equivalent), log-based detections, alerting and playbooks
• Run the finding-to-fix loop for security findings: triage, assign, fix, add a detection, retest
• Use LLMs and AI agents in security work: triaging findings, reviewing infrastructure changes, tuning detections, drafting incident timelines — and secure the agents themselves with scoped, short-lived permissions and audit trails
• Harden the supply chain: image signing and scanning, dependency policy, SBOMs
• Automate compliance evidence (CERT-In, ISO 27001, SOC 2, DPDP) together with the compliance team
• Set the security standards other engineers follow and review security-relevant changes
• Take part in on-call and lead security incidents
Requirements
• 5–9 years in DevOps, platform or security engineering, with at least 2 in a bank, fintech, payments company or other regulated environment
• Strong Kubernetes and Linux fundamentals; has run production clusters on at least one major cloud
• Hands-on with Terraform / OpenTofu and GitOps (ArgoCD or Flux)
• Has built security automation, not only operated tools: policy-as-code, secrets rotation, CI/CD security gates or detection pipelines
• Working knowledge of IAM, network security, TLS and secrets management across clouds
• Scripting and tooling in Python or Go
• Has been through security audits and knows what evidence auditors need
• Has built or used AI-based automation in infrastructure or security work, and understands the risks of AI agents: prompt injection, over-broad permissions, unreviewed actions
• Nice to have: Vault, SPIFFE / SPIRE, Falco or Tetragon, Cloudflare WAF, incident response lead experience, multi-cloud experience

title: SDE2 - API Platform
desc:
ABOUT THE ROLE
Sarvam's model APIs (LLM, ASR, TTS, Vision, Translate) are how developers and enterprises ship products on our foundation models. Our OpenAI-compatible LLM APIs route every request across multiple model deployments, with streaming, failover, metering, billing, and rate-limiting all part of the same stack. Today it's FastAPI and Python; we're in the middle of rewriting it in Go.
We're hiring a Software Engineer (SDE 2) to own core parts of this platform. The features. The reliability. The performance. This is an IC role.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
 - Building and evolving the LLM API platform, from the moment a request hits the edge to the response that goes back out
 - The Python→Go rewrite: building services in Go alongside the existing Python stack, without compromising reliability
 - Streaming infrastructure: SSE for Chat Completions and Responses, long-lived connections, clean handling of cancellations and client disconnects
 - Routing and failover: weighted provider chains, retries with backoff, and latency-driven admission control across model deployments
 - Protocol compatibility: keeping the API faithful to the OpenAI spec across inference servers (vLLM, SGLang, Dynamo) that each behave slightly differently
 - The commercial layer: metering, billing, and rate-limiting, engineered to the same bar as the model APIs themselves
 - Performance and reliability for a multi-tenant platform serving long-context agentic and coding workloads
 - Observability (logging, metrics, tracing), so the team can debug production confidently and quickly
 - Integration and load testing: the harness that lets us ship fast without breaking customer-facing APIs
 - Close partnership with the Inference and MLOps teams on production readiness for new model launches
 - Design-first, documentation-first engineering culture within the team: RFCs before code, decisions written down, no tribal knowledge
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
 - 3+ years building production backend systems
 - Strong Python in production: asyncio, FastAPI or similar, and services you've built and operated under real load
 - Working knowledge of Go, or a strong willingness to learn it: you'll work in both languages through the rewrite
 - Experience building low-latency, multi-tenant backend services
 - Hands-on experience with streaming systems: SSE or WebSockets, long-lived connections, backpressure
 - Strong PostgreSQL and Redis fundamentals: schema design, query performance, caching, and rate limiting
 - Comfort running services on Kubernetes in production
 - An ownership mindset: you test before you ship, debug production with metrics, logs, and traces, and write the RCA afterwards
BONUS POINTS

 - Familiarity with inference servers (vLLM, SGLang, Dynamo) and latency metrics such as time to first token and inter-token latency

desc:

ABOUT THE ROLE

You'll start with our marketing website: the homepage, product and use-case pages, interactive demos and calculators. You'll write production code, build reusable UI systems and turn rough ideas into polished interfaces, working closely with design, marketing and product engineering.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
 - Build the interface, not just the mockup. Write production-ready Astro and React components with thoughtful layouts, typography and responsive behaviour. Own the implementation from first prototype to the final browser-sized detail.
 - Build a UI system that holds together. Create reusable components, layout primitives and shared styles with clear APIs and sensible variants. Make the next page easier to build without turning every component into a 40-prop puzzle.
 - Make it feel right. Build interactions, transitions and animations that make interfaces clearer and more enjoyable. Think through keyboard use, loading, empty and error states, reduced motion and what happens when the happy path isn't so happy.
 - Prototype in code. Explore alternative layouts and interactions with designers, test ideas in the browser and refine the details together. You should be comfortable suggesting a better implementation, not waiting for every pixel and breakpoint to be specified.
 - Build the useful bits properly. Develop interactive demos, calculators and forms; connect thm to APIs and content. Handle state, validation, asynchronous behaviour and failures. Keep accessibility, performance, metadata and measurement working as part of what you ship.
 - Own the engineering quality. Make sound choices about component structure, rendering and hydration. Debug browser and performance issues, write appropriate tests, review code and check preview deployments. Ship maintainable changes that work beyond your own laptop.
 - Astro, React, TypeScript and CSS are at the core of the work. We use GitHub for code review and Railway for development and pull-request previews. Sanity, ImageKit and PostHog support content, media and measurement. You'll work with engineering on staging and production releases.
REQUIREMENTS
 - Have built and shipped interfaces you're proud to put your name on. Show us the actual thing, what you coded and the decisions you made. A live link beats a paragraph of adjectives.
 - Have strong HTML, CSS, JavaScript and TypeScript fundamentals and hands-on React experience. You can work effectively in Astro and reason about component composition, state, rendering and browser behaviour.
 - Have a good eye for visual design and the CSS skills to act on it. You care about spacing, type, hierarchy, responsive layouts and interaction details, and can turn that judgement into working code.
 - Can work across design and engineering. You're comfortable starting from a rough brief, prototyping options and discussing trade-offs with designers. You can also take an established design and implement it faithfully.
 - Can debug an unfamiliar frontend, integrate APIs and use Git, pull requests and automated checks confidently. You understand accessibility and web performance, and handle credentials and user data responsibly.
 - Use AI coding tools with judgement. Let them help you move faster. Read the diff, test the result and be able to explain what you're shipping. 'The model wrote it' isn't a debugging strategy.
 - Ask good questions when the brief is fuzzy. Explain trade-offs, suggest a practical way forward and use evidence before declaring that something needs fixing.
BONUS POINTS THAT ARE NOT DEALBREAKERS
 - You've built for B2B SaaS, developer tools or AI products.
 - You've built component libraries, design systems or interactive prototypes that other people actually use.
 - You've worked with animation, SVG, Canvas or other techniques that make complex ideas easier to explore on the web.
 - You've used a headless CMS such as Sanity, or worked on technical SEO and analytics integrations without letting them take over the frontend.
HOW TO APPLY
Skip the generic cover letter. Send us a couple of interfaces or web projects you've built, with a short note on what you personally designed and coded. Pick one and walk us through a component, interaction or tricky engineering decision. Code samples are welcome where you can share them.

title: Senior Software Engineer - Data Infrastructure
desc:
THE ROLE
Sarvam's products produce events, model traces, evals and billing data, and need to read that data back. The Data Platform team builds and runs the central data infrastructure every product uses: ingestion, streaming, the analytical warehouse, transformations, access control and audit.
We are hiring a Software Engineer / Senior Software Engineer (2–5 years of experience) to own this platform end to end. You will design, build and run systems that other teams depend on in production, and make real decisions on database internals, streaming and platform design. Stack: Go/Python, ClickHouse Cloud, Kafka, Avro, Airflow, dbt, Kubernetes, Terraform, AWS.
WHAT YOU'LL OWN & DO
 - Build and run the ingestion path: the service every product sends events to, Kafka behind it, and the pipes that land data in ClickHouse within seconds. Own schema validation, rate limits, dead-letter handling and the client SDKs.
 - Own the warehouse: ClickHouse Cloud. Design tables for the read path (sorting keys, partitions, materialized views, TTL), separate compute per workload, set per-user limits and per-tenant isolation, and attribute cost to the team that spent it.
 - Build reliable data pipelines and solve data problems: dbt models and Airflow DAGs with the BI engineers, CDC from product databases, sync and backfill jobs that are safe to re-run, and the data problems product teams bring you, such as a late source, a number that doesn't match or a query that has slowed down.
 - Make the platform self-serve: a registry of every dataset with its owner, schema, freshness and access; provisioning and permissions as code.
 - Run it in production: everything as Terraform and Helm with metrics, traces and alerts; be on call; handle incidents end to end, write the RCA and fix the root cause.
 - Grow the platform: new products keep arriving. You will help decide what the platform should do next and build it, whether that is a new source or sink, or a new way for teams to use the data.
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
 - 2–5 years of experience building, shipping and running large-scale, data-intensive systems in production, ideally at a startup where you owned things and were on call for them.
 - Deep expertise in at least one of: an OLAP database (ClickHouse preferred; Druid, BigQuery or Redshift also fine) or Kafka / event streaming. You understand how a columnar store writes, merges and scans data, or how a partitioned log gives ordering and delivery guarantees.
 - Experience with large-scale messaging systems like Kafka or RabbitMQ: partitions, consumer groups, delivery guarantees, backpressure.
 - Good at Go, or good at Python.
 - You know the usual data-system problems: schema evolution, idempotency, backpressure, partitioning, retention and TTL, CDC.
 - You have built or run at least one of: an event pipeline, a transformation layer (dbt, Spark or SQL on Airflow), a provisioning or control-plane service, or a multi-tenant data service with access control.
 - Comfortable with AWS, Kubernetes and Terraform in production.
 - You test before shipping, debug with metrics and traces, write RCAs, and document what you build.
 - Passion for data infrastructure and for enabling others by making their data easier to access.
NICE TO HAVE
 - ClickHouse in production: MergeTree, materialized views, projections, quotas, settings profiles, row policies, ClickHouse Cloud.
 - Kafka in depth: MSK, Kafka Connect, schema registry (Glue or Confluent), Avro.
 - dbt and Airflow at scale.
 - Audit or security data systems: append-only logs, integrity checks, tenant isolation.
 - OpenTelemetry, LLM observability (Langfuse or similar), eval pipelines.
 - Built an internal platform that other teams adopted.
